UserStory: As a new user, I want to create an account with a username, email, and password, so that I can access the app.
ExpectedBehavior: User can access sign-up form via 'Create an account' link in AccountSwitcher dialog. Form accepts username (3-50 chars), email, and password (≥8 chars). Form displays password requirements: min 8 chars and does not contain email. Password strength indicator shows weak/medium/strong based on length + digits + symbols. Submit button disabled until all fields valid and user online. On success, user signs in and dialog closes.
Notes: Accessed via AccountSwitcher dialog, not standalone page. Requires online connection (disabled when offline). Email requirement not enforced for server conflict; server returns 409 if user exists.
Permissions: Manage members/invites: project_lead(500); role changes: maintainer/owner(≥600); link role capped at contributor(400)

Feature: Login with username or email + password
UserStory: As an existing user, I want to sign in with my username or email and password, so that I can access my projects.
ExpectedBehavior: User navigates to /login or clicks 'Add another account' in AccountSwitcher. Login form accepts username/email and password. Show/hide password toggle (eye icon) reveals plaintext. Submit button disabled until both fields filled. On invalid credentials, shows 401 error 'Invalid username or password'. On success, user authenticated and redirected to ?next parameter or /. Offline state detected and submit disabled with message.
Notes: Two entry points: /login page (public route) and AccountSwitcher dialog. FrontierLoginForm supports optional onForgotPassword and returnTo props. Session persisted to IndexedDB and aq_hint=1 cookie set.
Permissions: No role required — public auth endpoints; account owner only for own session

UserStory: As a user logging in, I want to verify my password by toggling visibility, so that I can confirm I typed it correctly.
ExpectedBehavior: Login form password input type='password' by default. Eye icon button toggles to show password as plaintext (type='text'). Button aria-label changes from 'Show password' to 'Hide password'. Icon switches from Eye to EyeOff. Toggle can be clicked repeatedly.
Notes: Also present in signup and password reset forms for UX consistency.
Permissions: No role required — public auth endpoints; account owner only for own session

UserStory: As a user who forgot my password, I want to request a reset link, so that I can set a new password.
ExpectedBehavior: From login form, user clicks 'Forgot password?' link. Dialog switches to FrontierForgotPasswordForm with title 'Reset your password'. Form has email input (must match /.+@.+\.+/ pattern). 'Send reset link' button disabled until valid email. On submit, calls POST /api/v2/auth/password-reset/request { email }. Shows success message with email display and 'Back to login' button. Users can click 'Back to login' to return to login form without submitting.
Notes: Uses dummy-safe UX: success message shows 'If an account exists' to prevent email enumeration. Accessible from both /login page and AccountSwitcher 'Add account' dialog.
Permissions: No role required — public auth endpoints; account owner only for own session

UserStory: As a user with a reset link, I want to verify the link is valid before entering a new password, so that I know my reset request was legitimate.
ExpectedBehavior: User navigates to /reset-password?token=<token>&username=<username>. Page calls POST /api/v2/auth/password-reset/verify { token, username }. While verifying, shows 'Verifying link…' loading state. On 401/invalid: shows TokenExpiredView with form to request new link. On 200/valid: shows new password form. Form displays password checklist (8+ chars, not contain email). Submit button disabled until password valid.
Notes: Token expiry is handled server-side; client shows recovery UI (request new link) on error. Email optional in query string but shown if present.
Permissions: No role required — public auth endpoints; account owner only for own session

UserStory: As a user resetting my password, I want to set a new password and be automatically signed in, so that I can continue without clicking login again.
ExpectedBehavior: On /reset-password with valid token, user enters new password (≥8 chars). Form validates and shows checklist. On submit, calls POST /api/v2/auth/password-reset/reset { token, username, new_password }. On success, automatically calls login(username, new_password) to sign user in, then redirects to /. On 400/500 error, shows message and keeps user on form.
Notes: Automatic login after reset (line 215: await login) avoids friction of sign-in page.
Permissions: No role required — public auth endpoints; account owner only for own session

UserStory: As a user creating or resetting a password, I want to see password strength feedback, so that I can create a secure password.
ExpectedBehavior: Signup and reset forms display PasswordChecklist when user types. Shows green Check for 'At least 8 characters' when met. Shows Check for 'Does not contain your email' when met. Displays colored progress bar (red=weak 1/3, yellow=medium 2/3, green=strong full). Text label 'Strength: weak|medium|strong'. Strength calculated as: ≥8 chars (+1), ≥12 chars (+1), digits (+1), symbols (+1). Score ≤1=weak, 2=medium, ≥3=strong.
Notes: Checklist hidden if password field empty. Strength bar only shown when user has typed something.
Permissions: No role required — public auth endpoints; account owner only for own session

UserStory: As a user, I want my session to persist across page reloads, so that I don't need to log in repeatedly.
ExpectedBehavior: On successful login/register, FrontierSession (jwt, username, createdAt, email) saved to IndexedDB 'frontier' store with key 'envelope'. Session stored in envelope.sessions[username] and envelope.active set to username. On cold boot, loadActiveSession() retrieves session from IndexedDB. If session exists, user is logged in without re-authenticating. Session cleared only on logout.
Notes: Multi-account support: envelope tracks multiple sessions, only one active at a time. Legacy migration: reads old 'current' key format and upgrades to envelope model.
Permissions: No role required — public auth endpoints; account owner only for own session

Feature: Auth hint cookie for edge routing
UserStory: As a returning user, I want the Worker/edge to know I'm logged in without waiting for IndexedDB, so that the SPA loads quickly.
ExpectedBehavior: On successful login, IndexedDB write also sets aq_hint=1 cookie (Max-Age=31536000, Path=/, SameSite=Lax, no Domain). On logout, cookie deleted. On app boot, hasAuthHintCookie() checks if aq_hint=1 present. If no hint and not onboarded, RootRedirect sends hard window.location.replace('/homepage'). Hint scoped to host only (dev.aquilla.app vs aquilla.app vs localhost isolated).
Notes: Hint prevents flashing empty app shell at /homepage redirect. Non-credential cookie lets Worker decide routing without waiting for IDB.
Permissions: No role required — public auth endpoints; account owner only for own session

UserStory: As a user with multiple accounts, I want to see all my signed-in accounts in one place, so that I can switch between them or manage them.
ExpectedBehavior: AccountSwitcher button shows active user's avatar + username. Click opens dropdown showing 'Signed in' header, active account entry (with checkmark), list of other accounts (clickable to switch), 'Preferences' link, 'Add another account…' button, 'Log out' button. If >1 account, adds 'Sign out of all accounts' (destructive color). Clicking other account calls activateSession(), clears React Query cache and local project data. Clicking remove button (hover icon) on non-active account removes it.
Notes: Renders in header or sidebar variant. Dropdown closes on outside click or Escape. Switch clears query cache to prevent stale data from prior account.
Permissions: No role required — public auth endpoints; account owner only for own session

UserStory: As a user, I want to sign out, so that my account is no longer active on this device.
ExpectedBehavior: User clicks 'Log out' in AccountSwitcher. If outbox has pending edits, shows warning dialog with edit count and 'Log out anyway' button. On confirm or if no pending edits, clearSession() removes active session from IndexedDB, clears auth hint cookie, clears local project data, and wipes React Query cache. If other accounts exist, next account becomes active. App returns to login state.
Notes: Logout warns about pending outbox ops to prevent accidental data loss. If multiple accounts, next one promotes automatically (session-store line 119-122).
Permissions: No role required — public auth endpoints; account owner only for own session

UserStory: As a user with multiple logged-in accounts, I want to sign out globally, so that all my accounts are cleared from this device.
ExpectedBehavior: User clicks 'Sign out of all accounts' (only visible if >1 account). Shows warning about pending edits if any. On confirm, loops through all sessions and calls removeSession() for each, then clearAllLocalData() and query cache clear. All sessions removed from IndexedDB, auth hint cookie deleted. App returns to signed-out state.
Notes: Button only renders when sessions.length > 1. Uses destructive color variant. Same outbox warning as single logout.
Permissions: No role required — public auth endpoints; account owner only for own session

UserStory: As a user whose session expired while working, I want a non-intrusive notification, so that I can re-sign-in without losing context.
ExpectedBehavior: When any fetch helper receives 401 (expired session), it calls notifySessionExpired(). SessionExpiredBanner subscribes to signal, shows fixed top banner (amber, role=alert, aria-live=assertive) with message 'Your session expired. Sign in again to continue.' Banner has dismiss button (X icon). Banner clears on navigation or user dismiss. Shows link to /login?next=<current-path> to restore context.
Notes: Not a modal takeover; stays as banner while user can navigate. Signal pattern decouples fetch helpers from UI. Banner resets on navigation (line 28: useEffect on location.pathname).
Permissions: No role required — public auth endpoints; account owner only for own session

UserStory: As a developer testing the app, I want a one-click login shortcut, so that I don't manually enter credentials repeatedly.
ExpectedBehavior: Navigate to /__dev/login. If import.meta.env.DEV false, shows error 'dev login is disabled in production builds'. If DEV true, calls devLogin() which hits POST /__dev__/login on auth-worker. Returns mocked session with seeded dev user. On success, redirects to /project/dev-project. On 404 (WRANGLER_LOCAL not set), shows error 'dev login endpoint unavailable'. Cancellation-safe (cleanup on unmount).
Notes: Dev-only gated on import.meta.env.DEV. Endpoint requires WRANGLER_LOCAL=1 in auth-worker. Seeded project id hardcoded in auth-worker/src/routes/dev-seed.ts.
Permissions: No role required — public auth endpoints; account owner only for own session

UserStory: As a developer, I want a quick way to clear my session and return to onboarding, so that I can test the sign-in flow without manual cleanup.
ExpectedBehavior: Navigate to /__dev/logout. If import.meta.env.DEV true, calls logout() to clear session and redirect to /onboarding. If DEV false (production build), silently redirects to / with session intact. Dev route is no-op in built apps (verified by e2e in preview mode).
Notes: Gated on import.meta.env.DEV (line 18). Production gate verified: redirects to / without logout (line 19). E2E runs against built app (preview mode), so only tests !DEV branch.
Permissions: No role required — public auth endpoints; account owner only for own session

UserStory: As a user in private browsing, I want to know storage is unavailable, so that I understand why loads are slow.
ExpectedBehavior: PrivateModeBanner detects if OPFS unavailable (navigator.storage.getDirectory() throws in Safari private, Brave Tor, locked profiles). Shows one-time banner per session: 'Private browsing is restricting local storage…' with icon, message, and dismiss button. Banner stored per username+createdAt in sessionStorage. Dismissal persists for duration of session. Accessible state: role=alert not used (informational, not urgent).
Notes: Uses sessionStorage fallback when OPFS unavailable. Dismissal key includes username+createdAt to show banner per account per session. Waits for session ready (loading=false) to avoid flicker during transitions.
Permissions: Any authenticated user — scoped to own account

Feature: JWT token persistence and claims extraction
UserStory: As the app, I want to store the JWT and extract user info without validation, so that I know the canonical username and email.
ExpectedBehavior: On login, server returns access_token. Frontend decodes JWT payload (base64url to base64 conversion, JSON.parse) and extracts 'sub' (username) and 'email' claims without signature verification (server verified password). Falls back to login identifier if decode fails. Session stored with username from JWT sub claim, email from claim if present. Invalid/malformed tokens handled gracefully (returns empty {}).
Notes: No signature verification (server already verified). Base64url→base64 conversion at line 182. jwtClaims() returns safe interface; decode failures don't crash.
Permissions: No role required — public auth endpoints; account owner only for own session

UserStory: As the analytics system, I want to track auth events and attribute them to users, so that we can monitor signup/login patterns.
ExpectedBehavior: On login, computes distinct_id as SHA-256(username), calls posthog.identify(distinctId), and captures 'user logged in' event. On signup, same identify + capture 'user signed up' with email property (only if analytics consent given). On logout, captures 'user logged out' and calls posthog.reset().
Notes: Uses SHA-256 instead of username directly for privacy. Email property sent only if isAnalyticsEnabled() true. Reset on logout clears session identity.
Permissions: No role required — public auth endpoints; account owner only for own session

UserStory: As a user without internet, I want to see a message explaining why I can't sign in, so that I understand the issue.
ExpectedBehavior: FrontierLoginForm and FrontierSignupForm detect navigator.onLine and window online/offline events. When offline, shows alert message 'You're offline — connect to sign in' and disables submit button. When online again, button re-enables. Message dismisses on successful auth or stays on network error.
Notes: Submit button also checks !isOnline (line 99, 105). Message persists while offline, cleared on user action. Does not prevent form interaction, just disables submit.
Permissions: No role required — public auth endpoints; account owner only for own session

UserStory: As a new user, I want to see a branded welcome screen with the app logo and onboarding headline, so that I understand what I'm about to set up.
ExpectedBehavior: User lands at /onboarding route. WelcomeStep renders with app logo, headline (from branding config), subheading, and 'Get Started' button. Clicking 'Get Started' advances to step 2. Step indicator shows progress (Step 1 of 6).
Notes: Part of 6-step wizard; step 2 (PrivacyStep) is skipped if user has already set analytics consent in prior onboarding runs (line 39).
Permissions: Org owner (creator, 700) drives setup; tour visible to any authenticated user

UserStory: As a new user, I want to opt in or out of analytics sharing with a clear explanation, so that I control my data usage.
ExpectedBehavior: PrivacyStep renders with ShieldCheck icon, heading 'Help us improve', toggle switch for 'Share usage data'. Toggle defaults to enabled. If disabled, shows warning: 'With analytics disabled, we may not be able to help diagnose problems.' Clicking 'Continue' persists choice and advances to step 3. Back button returns to step 1. Footer includes link to /privacy-policy.
Notes: Persists to localStorage via useAnalyticsConsent hook. Step is skipped on revisits once any choice has been made (onboarding-done check on line 49).
Permissions: Org owner (creator, 700) drives setup; tour visible to any authenticated user

UserStory: As a new user, I want to sign in to my Frontier account (or create one) to unlock AI and sync features, so that I can collaborate and use cloud features.
ExpectedBehavior: SignInStep defaults to signup mode. Shows 'Create your Frontier account' heading. Renders FrontierSignupForm with onSuccess callback advancing to next step. User can toggle to 'Log in' mode (shows 'Sign in to Frontier'). In login mode, onSuccess calls onLoginComplete handler which checks for existing orgs: if user already has orgs, skips Name + Project steps and lands on dashboard; if brand-new account (no orgs), continues wizard. Password reset mode available ('Forgot password?'). 'Skip for now' button available in both signup and login modes. Dev mode (import.meta.env.DEV) shows 'Dev login' button. Back button returns to step 2. Once session is established, shows success screen: 'Signed in as [username]' with green checkmark and 'Continue' button.
Notes: onLoginComplete is AQU-282 feature: returning users skip Name + Project steps. Dev login requires WRANGLER_LOCAL=1 on auth-worker. Session is checked via useFrontierSession hook.
Permissions: Org owner (creator, 700) drives setup; tour visible to any authenticated user

UserStory: As a new user setting up my account, I want to enter my display name, so that my edits and comments are attributed to me across the project.
ExpectedBehavior: NameStep renders with heading 'What should we call you?' and description 'This name appears on your edits and comments.' Input field (id='display-name', placeholder='Anonymous translator') auto-focuses. Pre-fills from Frontier session.username if user hasn't typed anything yet. 'Continue' button saves name to localStorage key 'codex:username' (or defaults to 'Anonymous' if empty) and advances to step 4. Back button returns to step 3.
Notes: Skipped if user logs in and already has existing orgs (AQU-282).
Permissions: Org owner (creator, 700) drives setup; tour visible to any authenticated user

UserStory: As a new user, I want to create my first translation project with source and target languages, so that I have a project to start translating in.
ExpectedBehavior: ProjectStep renders form with heading 'Create your first project'. Three text inputs: Project name (placeholder 'My Translation Project'), Source language (placeholder 'English'), Target language (placeholder 'French'). Submit button reads 'Create Project' and is disabled until all three fields are non-empty. On submit, creates server project first (via createRemoteProject), then local IDB record (via createLocalProject). On success, advances to step 6 (ReadyStep). Shows 'Creating…' button state while busy. Errors are caught and displayed inline (e.g., 'Failed to create project.'). If no Frontier session JWT exists, shows alternate message: 'Sign in to create a project' with explanation that projects are server-only. 'Do this later' link skips project creation and advances to dashboard. Back button returns to step 3.
Notes: Skipped if user logs in and already has existing orgs (AQU-282). Server-side project creation must happen before local IDB to avoid 403 on access (AD-3 projects are server-only reads). Creates UUID for project.id via uuid() package.
Permissions: Manage members/invites: project_lead(500); role changes: maintainer/owner(≥600); link role capped at contributor(400)

UserStory: As a new user who just created a project, I want to see a success confirmation, so that I know I'm ready to start translating.
ExpectedBehavior: ReadyStep renders success state: green CheckCircle2 icon, heading 'You're all set!', message 'PROJECT_NAME is ready. We'll walk you through setting up AI and inviting collaborators next.' 'Start Translating' button navigates to project page at `/project/{projectId}` with router state `{ openSetupChecklist: true }`, triggering auto-open of setup checklist.
Notes: Marks localStorage 'codex:onboardingComplete' = 'true' and opens SetupChecklistDrawer via router state. Only shown when createdProject is non-null (step 6).
Permissions: Org owner (creator, 700) drives setup; tour visible to any authenticated user

UserStory: As a returning user, I want the app to remember I completed onboarding, so that I don't see the wizard again on subsequent visits.
ExpectedBehavior: Wizard sets localStorage 'codex:onboardingComplete' = 'true' when user completes (ReadyStep or skips ProjectStep). On subsequent visits, if this flag is set, user bypasses /onboarding and lands on dashboard (/). OnboardingWizard component is only mounted when token is absent or onboarding is incomplete.
Notes: Flag persists across sessions and browser profiles. Referenced in product tour auto-start logic (shouldAutoStartTour in useProductTour.ts).
Permissions: Org owner (creator, 700) drives setup; tour visible to any authenticated user

UserStory: As a new user who just completed onboarding, I want an interactive guided tour of the main workspace, so that I learn where everything is.
ExpectedBehavior: After onboarding completion (localStorage 'codex:onboardingComplete'='true') AND product tour not yet shown (localStorage 'codex:productTourDone'!='1'), ProductTour auto-starts with 600ms delay on first app render. User sees spotlight with semi-transparent backdrop and tooltip card overlaying key UI elements. Tour can be dismissed by clicking X, clicking 'Skip', pressing Escape, or completing all steps (clicking 'Done' on final step). Once dismissed, marked as done via localStorage and tour does not auto-start again.
Notes: AQU-243. 600ms delay allows sidebar/nav to render before trying to locate data-tour anchors. Auto-start happens once per browser profile. Call time is synchronous (wasProductTourDone/shouldAutoStartTour don't use React state) to avoid flash-then-start cycles.
Permissions: Org owner (creator, 700) drives setup; tour visible to any authenticated user

UserStory: As a user taking the product tour, I want to navigate between steps and see my progress, so that I can learn at my own pace.
ExpectedBehavior: Tour displays current step in a tooltip card with title, body text, and placement arrow (top/bottom/left/right, auto-repositioning if offscreen). Footer shows step progress dots (filled for current/past, empty for future). 'Back' button navigates to previous step (hidden on first step). 'Next' button advances to next step; on final step, reads 'Done' and closes tour. Step indicator reads 'Tour step N of M'. Keyboard shortcuts: Escape = skip, ArrowRight/Enter = next, ArrowLeft = previous.
Notes: Spotlight automatically repositions if anchor element moves (useEffect re-runs on window resize). Resolves visible steps each time tour opens to handle feature-gating (if anchor missing, step skipped).
Permissions: Any authenticated user — scoped to own account

UserStory: As a new user, I want to understand key workspace features through guided callouts, so that I can navigate and use the app effectively.
ExpectedBehavior: Tour displays 6 steps: (1) splash step centered on screen 'Welcome to your workspace', (2) org-switcher callout, (3) nav-overview (Projects) callout, (4) nav-assigned callout, (5) nav-settings callout, (6) account-switcher callout. Each step has title, body text, and preferred placement. Splash step has no arrow; others point to their target element with rounded-rect spotlight cutout.
Notes: TOUR_STEPS array is static. Each anchor references a data-tour attribute in the DOM (org-switcher, nav-overview, nav-assigned, nav-settings, account-switcher).
Permissions: Org owner (creator, 700) drives setup; tour visible to any authenticated user

UserStory: As a user taking the tour, I want to see the highlighted UI elements clearly with auto-positioned tooltips, so that I don't miss what's being explained.
ExpectedBehavior: Spotlight draws SVG cutout (rounded rect punch-out) around target element with 8px padding. Semi-transparent dark overlay fills remainder of screen. Tooltip card (288px wide, ~160px tall) positions itself relative to target using preferred placement (right/left/bottom/top) with 16px gap; auto-falls back to other sides if current choice doesn't fit viewport; final fallback centers on screen. Tooltip arrow points back to target (or no arrow for center-screen splash steps).
Notes: Rendered as SVG portal into document.body (z-index 9990-9991). Computes geometry on render, re-runs on window resize. If anchor element missing (feature-gated), step silently skipped.
Permissions: Org owner (creator, 700) drives setup; tour visible to any authenticated user

UserStory: As a returning user, I want to be able to restart the product tour, so that I can review features I may have forgotten.
ExpectedBehavior: OrgSidebar footer includes 'Take the tour' button or similar (accessible via useProductTourContext.openTour()). Clicking this button manually opens ProductTour even if it was already completed. Tour re-opens from step 1.
Notes: No local code read for OrgSidebar, but grep shows data-tour anchors are present there. Manual open does NOT reset the 'codex:productTourDone' flag — if user dismissed tour, clicking button opens it again but auto-start is still disabled.
Permissions: Org owner (creator, 700) drives setup; tour visible to any authenticated user

UserStory: As a user creating a first project, I want to see a setup checklist that guides me through configuration steps, so that I can set up AI, collaboration, and other features.
ExpectedBehavior: When user lands on project page after onboarding (ReadyStep navigates with router state openSetupChecklist=true), ProjectWorkspace opens SetupChecklistDrawer automatically. Checklist shows 4 items: Import files, Set translation instructions, Invite collaborators, Configure voice & transcription. Each item has title, description, completion dot (empty/filled), and collapsible body. Progress bar shows X of N complete. Checklist does not auto-open if: (1) user has already dismissed it for this project, (2) setup-auto-shown flag is set in localStorage for this project, (3) member list is still fetching, (4) AI model status is still resolving, OR (5) checklist is already complete (all 4 items done).
Notes: AQU-244. Per-project localStorage keys: codex:setupAutoShown.{projectId} (prevents re-opening on revisits), setupChecklistDismissed persisted on ProjectRecord. Auto-open logic in useSetupChecklist.shouldAutoOpen carefully avoids race conditions on project-switch by waiting for membersFetched + modelsResolved flags.
Permissions: Manage members/invites: project_lead(500); role changes: maintainer/owner(≥600); link role capped at contributor(400)

UserStory: As a user setting up a project, I want to import my source text files first, so that I can start working on translation.
ExpectedBehavior: Checklist item 'Import files' has body showing description and 'Import files' button. If files already imported, shows 'X files imported' and button changes to 'Import more files'. Clicking button closes drawer and opens parent's import dialog (ProjectWorkspace.onOpenImport). Item is marked complete when project.files.length > 0.
Notes: Does not auto-complete the step — user must explicitly import files. Completion derived from fileCount > 0.
Permissions: Source content edits: project_lead(500)

UserStory: As a user setting up a project, I want to customize translation instructions for the AI, so that suggestions match my project's style and domain.
ExpectedBehavior: Checklist item 'Set translation instructions' expands to show textarea with system prompt. Defaults to DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT (imported from useCompletionSettings). User can edit prompt; character count displayed at bottom. 'Reset to default' button (disabled if already at default). 'Save instructions' button saves to project.completionSettings.systemPrompt and marks item complete. Prompt supports placeholders {sourceLanguage} and {targetLanguage} (shown as code snippets in UI). Item completed when systemPrompt is non-empty and not the default.
Notes: Also accessible via SystemPromptNudge banner in workspace (shown 24h after project creation if still using default). Placeholder substitution happens at inference time.
Permissions: Org owner (creator, 700) drives setup; tour visible to any authenticated user

UserStory: As a user setting up a project, I want to invite teammates to collaborate, so that we can work on translation together.
ExpectedBehavior: Checklist item 'Invite collaborators' expands to show InviteStep UI with two invitation paths: (1) Invite by Aquilla username — text input + 'Add' button, adds user directly to project_members server-side as 'contributor' role; (2) Share link — 'Create link' button generates server-backed invite token, displays /join/{token} URL, 'Copy' button copies to clipboard, 'Create another link' button generates new token. Input disabled if user not signed in (Frontier JWT missing). Item completed when memberCount > 0 (other project members, excluding self). Both paths trigger onSharesChanged callback to refresh member list.
Notes: Requires Frontier session JWT for both paths. Errors handled inline (e.g., 'No Aquilla user named X'). Share link redirection handled via /join/:token route.
Permissions: Manage members/invites: project_lead(500); role changes: maintainer/owner(≥600); link role capped at contributor(400)

UserStory: As a user setting up a project, I want to configure local AI models for voice and transcription, so that I can use offline features without managing large downloads upfront.
ExpectedBehavior: Checklist item 'Configure voice & transcription' starts collapsed; expands to show two sections: Transcription (Whisper checkbox, 140 MB) and Voice generation (radio group: None, Gemini with API key input, Kokoro local, MMS multilingual). Each model option shows label, size, status indicator (Ready/Failed/Downloading N%), and blurb. Selecting Gemini shows nested API key input (password field, saved on blur). Download size shown in amber warning banner. 'Download ~X MB' button (disabled if nothing selected, all-ready, or already downloading) kicks off prefetchAiModels for selected models in background. Download status shown in AiModelDownloadChip (floating bottom-left pill with progress bars). Item completed when all selected models are ready.
Notes: Downloads are optional and non-blocking. Default: nothing pre-selected to avoid surprising large downloads. Models persisted in browser IndexedDB and managed by useModelStatus hook. Requires user to first accept AI consent via AiModelConsentDialog (global, once per browser).
Permissions: Org owner (creator, 700) drives setup; tour visible to any authenticated user

UserStory: As a user, I want to see what's planned for future project setup features, so that I have visibility into roadmap.
ExpectedBehavior: Checklist shows two placeholder items: 'Upload project standards' and 'Import glossary / translation memory', both marked 'Coming soon' badge, with dashed border and reduced opacity (opacity-60). Items are non-interactive (no click handler).
Notes: Placeholder UI only; no implementation behind these features.
Permissions: Org owner (creator, 700) drives setup; tour visible to any authenticated user

UserStory: As a user, I want to see my progress through setup and know when I'm done, so that I feel guided through the onboarding experience.
ExpectedBehavior: Progress bar at top updates as items are completed. Text shows 'N of M complete'. When all items complete, 'Skip for now' button changes to 'All set' with green CheckCircle icon and message 'You can reopen this checklist any time from the project header.' Drawer can still be dismissed before completion ('Skip for now' button).
Notes: Checklist items auto-collapse when marked complete (ChecklistItem self-collapses on complete transition). Dismissal persists setupChecklistDismissed flag on ProjectRecord.
Permissions: Org owner (creator, 700) drives setup; tour visible to any authenticated user

UserStory: As a user, I want to expand and collapse checklist items, so that I can focus on one step at a time.
ExpectedBehavior: Each ChecklistItem is a collapsible accordion row. Clicking title row toggles open/closed state. When complete prop transitions false→true, item auto-collapses (so next incomplete item gets focus). Chevron icon rotates 90° to indicate open state. Open item shows full body content.
Notes: Auto-collapse is a UX pattern to guide user to next incomplete step; does not require parent to manage open state.
Permissions: Org owner (creator, 700) drives setup; tour visible to any authenticated user

UserStory: As a user who skipped customizing AI instructions and has content in their project, I want a gentle reminder to set up the system prompt, so that I get better translations.
ExpectedBehavior: Once per day (24h after project creation), if: project has files with content (cellCount > 0), system prompt is still default or empty, and user hasn't dismissed nudge yet (defaultPromptNudgeDismissedAt not set), a banner appears at top of workspace editor showing Sparkles icon and message 'Your AI is still using the default translation instructions. Customize them to match your project's tone and domain — shared with everyone on the project.' 'Customize' button opens project settings or AI instructions dialog. X button dismisses and marks defaultPromptNudgeDismissedAt. Dismissed flag persists on ProjectRecord, preventing re-show.
Notes: Soft nudge, not part of required setup path. NUDGE_DELAY_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000. shouldShowSystemPromptNudge checks all conditions before rendering.
Permissions: Org owner (creator, 700) drives setup; tour visible to any authenticated user

UserStory: As a user about to use local AI features for the first time, I want to consent to model download and understand the tradeoffs, so that I'm informed about bandwidth and privacy.
ExpectedBehavior: Global dialog (mounted once at app root) listens to pendingAiConsent via global ai-consent service. When a feature (TTS, ASR) needs to download its first model in this browser, dialog opens with heading 'Download {model.label}?' and description including model size (MB) and rationale. Three buttons: 'Cancel' (rejects consent, feature fails), 'Just [Model Name]' (grants consent for this model only), 'Enable all local models' (grants consent for all, pre-downloads whisper + kokoro + mms in background while dialog closes). Footer note 'You'll only see this prompt once per browser.' Download progress shown in background via AiModelDownloadChip.
Notes: Global consent gate; resolves with Promise when user makes choice. Non-blocking — if user clicks Cancel, feature gracefully fails. If 'Enable all', prefetchAiModels runs in background (.catch suppressed).
Permissions: Org owner (creator, 700) drives setup; tour visible to any authenticated user

UserStory: As a user with local models downloading, I want to see live download progress, so that I know the feature is working and can estimate completion time.
ExpectedBehavior: Floating chip appears at bottom-left of screen (z-index 30, above most UI but below modals). Shows Spinner icon and 'Downloading AI models' title. Lists each model being downloaded with label and percentage (e.g., 'Whisper 45%'), progress bar under each. When all models finish, briefly flashes 'AI models ready' with CheckCircle icon for ~4s, then auto-hides. If error occurs, shows AlertCircle and model name + error message, with 'Retry' button. User can dismiss chip with X button (re-appears if new error happens). While downloading, footer note 'Runs in the background — you can keep working as normal.'
Notes: Uses useModelStatus hook to track whisper/kokoro/mms status. Ready flash (green confirmation) auto-clears after READY_FLASH_MS (4s). Auto re-shows on new errors (to alert user that manual retry is needed).
Permissions: Org owner (creator, 700) drives setup; tour visible to any authenticated user

UserStory: As a user with multiple organizations, I want to see all my organizations, so that I can understand my workspace portfolio.
ExpectedBehavior: When a user has 2+ orgs, OrgContext computes isAllOrgs=true (orgs.length > 1 && activeOrgId == null). The dashboard renders 'All organizations' as the workspace label. A grid card shows the count of organizations. The OrgSwitcher dropdown shows 'All organizations' as an option (line 100-105, OrgSwitcher.tsx). Users can click 'All organizations' in the switcher to navigate to this view via ?org=all query param.
Notes: Only visible when user has 2+ orgs; if only 1 org exists, isAllOrgs remains false.
Permissions: Switch/view: any org member; create/rename/manage org: org owner/admin (≥600)

UserStory: As a user with multiple organizations, I want to switch between them quickly, so that I can work on different org workspaces.
ExpectedBehavior: OrgSwitcher renders a dropdown button (ChevronsUpDown icon) showing current org name + role, or 'All organizations' if in all-orgs view. Clicking the button toggles open state. Dropdown lists each org as a clickable row with role subtitle and a checkmark on the active one. Selecting an org calls setActiveOrg(orgId), stores it in localStorage as org:active, and navigates to ?org={orgId}. The context emits the new activeOrgId.
Notes: Requires 2+ orgs to show. Single-org users see no switcher (line 28, OrgSwitcher.tsx: !activeOrg && !isAllOrgs returns null).
Permissions: Switch/view: any org member; create/rename/manage org: org owner/admin (≥600)

UserStory: As a user, I want to create a new organization, so that I can manage a separate workspace.
ExpectedBehavior: In OrgSwitcher dropdown, a '+ Create org' button appears at the bottom (line 178-184, OrgSwitcher.tsx). Clicking it reveals an input[aria-label='New org name'] + Create button. User types an org name and clicks Create. The createOrg(jwt, name) API call fires (lib/frontier/orgs.ts:115). On success, org list refreshes and the new org becomes active. The switcher trigger updates to show the new org name. If create fails, error bubbles (currently caught but not displayed in createName form state).
Notes: Creating is available to all authenticated users. Server-side enforcement is implicit (POST /api/v2/orgs requires auth).
Permissions: Switch/view: any org member; create/rename/manage org: org owner/admin (≥600)

UserStory: As an org owner/admin, I want to rename my organization inline, so that I can update the workspace name without navigating away.
ExpectedBehavior: In OrgSwitcher dropdown, a 'Rename' button appears (visible only when activeOrg?.role.level >= 600, line 31, OrgSwitcher.tsx). Clicking 'Rename' shows input[aria-label='Rename org'] prefilled with current name + Save button. User edits and clicks Save. renameOrg(jwt, activeOrg.id, newName) API fires. On success, context refreshes orgs and the switcher trigger updates to show the new name. Form clears and closes.
Notes: Role-gated: requires level >= 600 (owner/admin). When not owner, button does not render.
Permissions: Switch/view: any org member; create/rename/manage org: org owner/admin (≥600)

UserStory: As an org user, I want to see my organization's projects on a dashboard, so that I can browse and filter translation work.
ExpectedBehavior: OrgHome renders at / when jwt is set and an org is selected (activeOrgId != null && !isAllOrgs). The page displays: org name as h1 heading (line 420, OrgHome.tsx), a rollup strip with stat cards (Projects, Avg translated %, Avg validated %, Avg audio %, Stalled count, Overdue count), a project list filtered by status and search query, and org-specific panels (WorkloadRollup, UsageRollup, CreditsPanel). When jwt is null, shows unauthenticated message with Sign in link.
Notes: Loads portfolio data via getPortfolio(jwt, activeOrgId) once per org change. Displays 'No projects in this org yet' when portfolio is empty.
Permissions: Switch/view: any org member; create/rename/manage org: org owner/admin (≥600)

UserStory: As a user with multiple orgs, I want to see a dashboard across all my organizations, so that I can monitor progress holistically.
ExpectedBehavior: When isAllOrgs=true (activeOrgId == null && orgs.length > 1), OrgHome renders a distinct cross-org layout. Top section shows 6 stat cards: org count, project count, avg translated %, avg validated %, stalled count, overdue count. Below: left grid shows Organizations section (filterable list of org cards with per-org stats), right grid shows Projects section (all projects across all orgs, filterable by name/status, sortable by lens). Each org card is clickable and opens that org's dashboard.
Notes: Loads via getPortfolios(jwt, orgIds) for all orgs. Only shown when 2+ orgs exist. Organization cards show project count, avg translated %, avg validated %, stalled count, and overdue count.
Permissions: Switch/view: any org member; create/rename/manage org: org owner/admin (≥600)

UserStory: As a user with many organizations, I want to search/filter orgs by name, so that I can find a specific org quickly.
ExpectedBehavior: When viewing 'All organizations' (isAllOrgs=true), an input[placeholder='Filter organizations…'] appears above the org list (line 492-500, OrgHome.tsx). User types; orgs are filtered client-side by name (case-insensitive includes check, line 347-350). Empty result shows 'No matching organizations.' message. Clearing the input restores the full list.
Notes: Only available in 'All organizations' view. Filter is local state (orgQuery), no API call.
Permissions: Switch/view: any org member; create/rename/manage org: org owner/admin (≥600)

UserStory: As an org user, I want to filter projects by name, so that I can quickly find a project to work on.
ExpectedBehavior: On org dashboard, input[placeholder='Filter projects…', aria-label='Filter projects by name'] is present. User types a query; projects are filtered client-side (case-insensitive includes, line 382, OrgHome.tsx). When a filter is active and no projects match, shows 'No matching projects.' Empty result message changes based on the active project lens (e.g., 'No recently updated projects yet.'). Clear button (X icon) appears when input has text (line 563-573).
Notes: Filter only narrows the project list display; rollup stats above remain for the full portfolio (not filtered).
Permissions: Switch/view: any org member; create/rename/manage org: org owner/admin (≥600)

UserStory: As an org user, I want to filter projects by status, so that I can focus on problematic or active projects.
ExpectedBehavior: Status filter pills appear on org dashboard when projects exist (line 576-595, OrgHome.tsx): All (default), Stalled, Overdue. Each pill has aria-pressed attribute. Clicking a pill sets statusFilter state and updates aria-pressed. 'Stalled' shows projects with no recent activity (14+ days, activityStatus=stalled). 'Overdue' shows projects past their deadline. 'All' shows all projects. Filter integrates with name search (both must match).
Notes: Status filter is only visible when projects.length > 0 (line 736, OrgHome.tsx). 'Stalled' is a local calc (14 days idle), not a server-side status.
Permissions: Switch/view: any org member; create/rename/manage org: org owner/admin (≥600)

Feature: Sort projects by lens (Recently updated/Needs attention/Least translated/Most progress/Name)
UserStory: As an org user, I want to sort projects by different criteria, so that I can view work in order of priority or progress.
ExpectedBehavior: A 'Sort by' dropdown appears in the filter bar (line 786-807, OrgHome.tsx, using Select component). Options: Recently updated, Needs attention, Least translated, Most progress, Name. Default is 'Recently updated'. Selection is persisted to localStorage (PROJECT_LENS_STORAGE_KEY, line 38). Each lens applies a specific sort algorithm: 'recent' by lastEditAt desc, 'attention' by attentionRank desc, 'least-translated' by translatedPct asc, 'most-progress' by translatedPct desc, 'name' by alphabetical. Empty state message varies by lens.
Notes: Project lens is only available in single-org view; 'All organizations' view has its own simpler sorting. Lens choice is remembered per browser via localStorage.
Permissions: Switch/view: any org member; create/rename/manage org: org owner/admin (≥600)

UserStory: As a user, I want to see incoming project invitations addressed to my email, so that I can discover invites that may not have arrived via email.
ExpectedBehavior: On org dashboard, if pendingInvites.length > 0 (fetched by listMyPendingInvites, line 280, OrgHome.tsx), a 'Pending invitations' section appears (line 426-451). Each invite row shows project name(s), inviter, role, expiry date (if set), and a 'Review & accept' link to /join/:token. Section is org-independent (not scoped to activeOrgId). Unauthenticated users do not see this section.
Notes: Feature AQU-326. Invites are fetched without org scope (email-matched). Only appears when there are unredeemed invites.
Permissions: Manage members/invites: project_lead(500); role changes: maintainer/owner(≥600); link role capped at contributor(400)

Feature: View shared projects (cross-org access via invite link)
UserStory: As a user who has accepted a project invite from another org, I want to see that project on my dashboard, so that I can access projects shared with me.
ExpectedBehavior: Below the org's own project list, if sharedProjects.length > 0 (from partitionSharedProjects, line 330, OrgHome.tsx), a 'Shared with you' section appears (line 882-898). Each shared project shows name, role badge, and links to /projects/:id. Shared projects come from cross-org grant paths (invite link, bulk add) and are not part of the current org's portfolio. If no shared projects exist, section is hidden.
Notes: Feature AQU-335. Only visible in single-org view, not in 'All organizations' view. Requires fetchAccessibleProjects API (cross-org discovery).
Permissions: Manage members/invites: project_lead(500); role changes: maintainer/owner(≥600); link role capped at contributor(400)

UserStory: As an org user, I want to see which projects are overdue or due soon, so that I can prioritize urgent work.
ExpectedBehavior: On each project row, if project has a deadline, deadlineStatus(project, now) returns 'overdue', 'soon', or null. Matching projects show status chips: red 'Overdue' badge or amber 'Due soon' badge (line 667-676, OrgHome.tsx). Overdue projects are included in overdueCount stat card. The 'Overdue' status filter shows only projects with 'overdue' status.
Notes: Status is calculated from portfolio project deadline property. Must be set via project settings.
Permissions: Switch/view: any org member; create/rename/manage org: org owner/admin (≥600)

UserStory: As an org user, I want to know which projects have stalled (no activity for 14+ days), so that I can re-engage with inactive work.
ExpectedBehavior: For each project, activityStatus(project, now) returns 'stalled' if lastEditAt is null or older than 14 days (STALE_THRESHOLD_MS = 14 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000, line 30, OrgHome.tsx). Projects with 'stalled' status show warning text in the right-hand status column (line 691, OrgHome.tsx: 'Stalled' in red destructive color). Stalled projects are counted in stalledCount stat card. The 'Stalled' status filter option (now labeled 'Active' in pill group) may appear in future (currently 'All/Stalled/Overdue', line 56-60).
Notes: 'Not started' projects (no lastEditAt and no translated cells) are distinguished from 'stalled' (line 122). Only 'stalled' projects show the stalled status text.
Permissions: Switch/view: any org member; create/rename/manage org: org owner/admin (≥600)

UserStory: As an org user, I want to see translation and validation progress for each project at a glance, so that I can assess completion status.
ExpectedBehavior: On each project row, two horizontal progress bars render (line 682-687, OrgHome.tsx): amber bar for translated %, emerald bar for validated %. Bar width reflects percentage of translated or validated cells. Aria-label summarizes both percentages. Right-hand status column shows numerical percentages (e.g., '75% validated'). Progress data comes from portfolio project metrics (translatedPct, validatedPct helpers).
Notes: Audio % is also shown in right-hand column. Bars are visual representations of portfolio data.
Permissions: Switch/view: any org member; create/rename/manage org: org owner/admin (≥600)

UserStory: As an org admin, I want to see aggregated statistics across all org projects, so that I can monitor overall progress and health.
ExpectedBehavior: On org dashboard, a strip of 6 stat cards appears (line 708-733, OrgHome.tsx, single-org view; or line 456-480, multi-org view): Projects (count), Avg translated %, Avg validated %, Avg audio %, Stalled (count), Overdue (count). Stats are computed from the loaded portfolio (averagePct helper, or direct counts for stalled/overdue). All stats have centered text layout with bold number + small label. Overdue count is red if > 0. Multi-org view shows these plus org count.
Notes: Stats are never filtered by search/status (they always reflect the full portfolio). Only visible when org has loaded (not during initial load spinner).
Permissions: Switch/view: any org member; create/rename/manage org: org owner/admin (≥600)

UserStory: As an org owner, I want to create a new project from the dashboard, so that I can set up translation work quickly.
ExpectedBehavior: On org dashboard header (line 400-406, OrgHome.tsx), a ProjectCreateDialog button appears when activeOrgId != null. Clicking opens a dialog to create a project. On success, handleCreated navigates to /projects/:id. If no org is selected (activeOrgId == null), a disabled hint appears: 'Select an organization to create a project'.
Notes: ProjectCreateDialog is a separate component. Disabled state prevents accidental project creation in wrong org.
Permissions: Lifecycle ops: project_lead(500)+ / owner(700)

UserStory: As an org admin, I want to see org-specific workload, usage, and credit information, so that I can manage org resources.
ExpectedBehavior: Below the project list in single-org view, three panels render conditionally (line 902-910, OrgHome.tsx) when jwt is set, not in isAllOrgs mode, and activeOrgId != null: WorkloadRollup (project team assignment info), UsageRollup (usage metrics), CreditsPanel (credit balance and purchasing, role-gated to >= level 600 via orgRoleLevel prop). These panels are hidden in multi-org 'All organizations' view.
Notes: These panels make API calls independently. CreditsPanel is role-gated (org owner only).
Permissions: Switch/view: any org member; create/rename/manage org: org owner/admin (≥600)

UserStory: As an org user, I want a sidebar with org-scoped navigation, so that I can access org pages (projects, teams, members, settings) easily.
ExpectedBehavior: OrgSidebar renders (AppShell sidebar prop). Top shows OrgSwitcher (org/all-org selection). Below: nav links to /projects (Projects), and org-scoped routes when not isAllOrgs: /teams (Teams), /assigned (Assigned to me). Admin-only routes (when role.level >= 600): /members (Members), /projects/archived (Archived), /settings (Settings). Platform admin route: /admin (Admin). Bottom: 'Take the tour' button + AccountSwitcher.
E2ESpec: none (navigation is implicit in other e2e specs)
Notes: NavLinks use end={true} to activate only on exact match. Data-tour attributes support product tour (AQU-243).
Permissions: Platform-admin only (isPlatformAdminUsername allowlist)

UserStory: As an org user, I want breadcrumbs showing my org context, so that I understand where I am in the navigation hierarchy.
ExpectedBehavior: OrgBreadcrumb renders (AppShell header). Displays crumb sequence: 'All organizations' › org-name › section-name (e.g., 'Projects', 'Teams'). 'All organizations' breadcrumb is clickable and navigates to ?org=all when orgs.length > 1 and not isAllOrgs. Org name is clickable (navigates /) only when not on the Projects page (canNavigateToOrg logic, line 15, OrgBreadcrumb.tsx). Section only shows if section !== 'Projects' or parent exists.
Notes: Breadcrumb is a header complement to OrgSwitcher. Logic prevents navigation loops (e.g., Projects › Projects › Projects).
Permissions: Switch/view: any org member; create/rename/manage org: org owner/admin (≥600)

UserStory: As a user with only one org, I want that org to be automatically selected, so that I see the org dashboard without extra navigation.
ExpectedBehavior: On OrgProvider mount or org list refresh, if orgs.length === 1, activeOrgId is set to orgs[0].id automatically (line 49, OrgContext.tsx). If already at / (org home), the dashboard shows that org's projects. User does not see 'All organizations' view (isAllOrgs=false, line 92).
Notes: Reduces friction for single-org users. Multi-org users start with activeOrgId=null (isAllOrgs=true if > 1 org).
Permissions: Switch/view: any org member; create/rename/manage org: org owner/admin (≥600)

UserStory: As an org user, I want my selected org to be remembered across sessions, so that I return to my preferred workspace.
ExpectedBehavior: OrgProvider stores activeOrgId in localStorage (key 'org:active', line 8, OrgContext.tsx) on every setActiveOrg/setAllOrgs call. On mount, the stored value is read and set as initial activeOrgId (line 32-37). If the stored value is 'all', activeOrgId remains null (isAllOrgs logic). Invalid or missing values default to null.
Notes: Storage is guarded with try-catch (line 33-37). Sync between tabs uses OrgContext subscribers only; no cross-tab sync.
Permissions: Switch/view: any org member; create/rename/manage org: org owner/admin (≥600)

Feature: Sync org selection with URL query param
UserStory: As an org user, I want URL-based org selection (shareable/bookmarkable), so that org context persists in links.
ExpectedBehavior: OrgContext watches location.search (line 67-80, OrgContext.tsx). If pathname === '/' and ?org={value}, the org ID is extracted and set as activeOrgId, stored in localStorage. Value 'all' sets activeOrgId to null (isAllOrgs mode). Invalid values are ignored. OrgSwitcher and OrgBreadcrumb navigate with ?org= when switching orgs (line 38, 45, 21, OrgBreadcrumb.tsx).
Notes: URL-based selection is the source of truth when at /; localStorage is a fallback.
Permissions: Switch/view: any org member; create/rename/manage org: org owner/admin (≥600)

Feature: Handle session expiration in org context
UserStory: As a user whose session expires, I want the app to notify me and halt org operations, so that I re-authenticate.
ExpectedBehavior: When OrgContext or OrgHome fetch calls encounter a UserError with category='session-expired' (e.g., 401 from listMyOrgs or getPortfolio), notifySessionExpired() is called (line 56, OrgContext.tsx; line 216, 246, OrgHome.tsx). This emits a SessionExpiredSignal that triggers a toast/redirect to login. Error state is set but rendering continues (gracefully handling stale data).
E2ESpec: none (session expiry is infrastructure-level, not testable in normal E2E)
Notes: Session-expired errors are distinguished from other API errors (e.g., network timeouts) to provide targeted feedback.
Permissions: Switch/view: any org member; create/rename/manage org: org owner/admin (≥600)

UserStory: As a user with network issues, I want error messages about org loading, so that I understand why the dashboard is unavailable.
ExpectedBehavior: If listMyOrgs or getPortfolio fails (network, 5xx, timeout), error state is captured (line 58, OrgContext.tsx; line 218, OrgHome.tsx). OrgHome displays error text in red (line 415, OrgHome.tsx): 'Something went wrong: [error message]'. User can retry via refresh (explicit or via automatic navigation). Error does not render fake empty state.
Notes: Errors are displayed inline, not as modal dialogs. User must navigate away and back to clear the error (no error dismissal UI).
Permissions: Switch/view: any org member; create/rename/manage org: org owner/admin (≥600)

UserStory: As a user with many orgs, I want to search within the org switcher, so that I can find the right org quickly.
ExpectedBehavior: OrgSwitcher dropdown renders a list of org items (line 107-121, OrgSwitcher.tsx). While no native search box is implemented in the switcher, the dropdown is scrollable (max-h-60 overflow-y-auto, line 91) and labeled with org role subtitle for quick visual scanning.
Notes: Search within the switcher is not implemented; users must scroll or use browser Find. OrgHome has org search in the 'All organizations' view (separate from switcher).
Permissions: Switch/view: any org member; create/rename/manage org: org owner/admin (≥600)

UserStory: As a visitor without an account, I want to know I'm signed out, so that I can sign in.
ExpectedBehavior: When sessionLoading completes and jwt is null (line 288, OrgHome.tsx), instead of rendering project cards, a centered message appears: 'Sign in to see your workspace' + 'Your session has ended or you are not signed in...' + a blue 'Sign in' button linking to /login?next=/. No rollup stats, no project list, no spinner.
Notes: This is a graceful fallback for unauthenticated visitors. No fake-empty cards are rendered to avoid confusion.
Permissions: Switch/view: any org member; create/rename/manage org: org owner/admin (≥600)

Feature: Org role display (in switcher and sidebar)
UserStory: As an org user, I want to see my role within each org, so that I understand my permissions.
ExpectedBehavior: In OrgSwitcher dropdown, each org item shows role.name (with underscores replaced by spaces, line 116, OrgSwitcher.tsx) as a small subtitle below the org name. In OrgHome rollup, org items in the 'All organizations' grid show a role badge (line 523-525, OrgHome.tsx) with the role name. Role affects available features: 'owner' / 'maintainer' (level >= 600) unlock rename + admin pages.
Notes: Role names are normalized (underscores → spaces) for display. Role level (numeric) is used for permission checks; name is for display only.
Permissions: Switch/view: any org member; create/rename/manage org: org owner/admin (≥600)

UserStory: As an org user, I want to know if I can perform org actions (invite, settings), so that I don't attempt prohibited operations.
ExpectedBehavior: Rename button in OrgSwitcher is visible only when role.level >= 600 (line 31, OrgSwitcher.tsx). OrgSidebar shows Members/Archived/Settings links only when role.level >= 600 (line 45-50, OrgSidebar.tsx). CreditsPanel visibility is gated the same way (line 908, OrgHome.tsx). Non-admins see stripped-down sidebar (Projects, Teams, Assigned to me only).
E2ESpec: none (permission display is implicit in page rendering)
Notes: This is UI-side gating only; server enforces actual permissions. Users can't reach forbidden pages via direct URL (server returns 403).
Permissions: Manage members/invites: project_lead(500); role changes: maintainer/owner(≥600); link role capped at contributor(400)

UserStory: As an org admin, I want to manually refresh the org list, so that I see newly created orgs or membership changes immediately.
ExpectedBehavior: OrgContext exposes a refresh() function (line 41-63, OrgContext.tsx) that re-fetches listMyOrgs and updates state. Callers can invoke refresh() directly (e.g., OrgSwitcher does after createOrg, line 54). If called during an active render, the new org list replaces the old one. If no orgs exist after refresh, activeOrgId is set to null.
Notes: refresh() is called automatically on OrgProvider mount and on JWT changes. Manual refresh is typically triggered after mutations (create, rename).
Permissions: Switch/view: any org member; create/rename/manage org: org owner/admin (≥600)

UserStory: As an org admin, I want to see all teams in my organization with member/project counts, so that I can manage team structure and composition.
ExpectedBehavior: Navigate to /teams. Page loads with grid of team cards showing team name, member count, project count, and 'Member' badge if user is in team. When no teams exist, show 'No teams in this org yet.' message. When org not selected, show 'Select an organization' prompt.
Notes: Org-scoped to activeOrgId. Only visible when authenticated with Frontier session.
Permissions: View members: viewer(100); add/remove members & assign: project_lead(500); change roles: maintainer/owner(≥600)

UserStory: As an org admin with many teams, I want to search teams by name, so that I can quickly find a specific team.
ExpectedBehavior: On /teams page when teams exist, a search input (type=search, placeholder='Search teams…') appears. Typing filters teams by case-insensitive name substring match. Empty search shows all teams. When no teams match, show 'No teams match "[query]"' with a 'Clear' button.
Permissions: View members: viewer(100); add/remove members & assign: project_lead(500); change roles: maintainer/owner(≥600)

Feature: Sort teams by name, member count, or project count
UserStory: As an org admin, I want to sort teams by different metrics, so that I can prioritize attention on larger/busier teams.
ExpectedBehavior: On /teams page when teams exist, a Select dropdown appears with 3 options: 'Name (A–Z)', 'Members (most first)', 'Projects (most first)'. Default is 'Name'. Sorting is applied instantly to the displayed list.
Notes: Sorting is in-memory on the client; no server-side sort parameter.
Permissions: View members: viewer(100); add/remove members & assign: project_lead(500); change roles: maintainer/owner(≥600)

UserStory: As an org admin, I want to create a new team, so that I can group members and grant them project access together.
ExpectedBehavior: On /teams page, an admin sees a 'New team' button. Clicking it reveals an inline form with 'Team name' (required) and 'Description (optional)' inputs plus 'Create' and 'Cancel' buttons. Submitting POSTs to /api/v2/orgs/:orgId/groups, navigates to /teams/:groupId on success. Non-admins (level < 600) do not see the button.
Notes: Admin-only (maintainer+ required, level 600+). Description is optional in both form and API.
Permissions: View members: viewer(100); add/remove members & assign: project_lead(500); change roles: maintainer/owner(≥600)

UserStory: As an org admin, I want to see all members and projects assigned to a team, so that I can understand the team's scope and composition.
ExpectedBehavior: Navigate to /teams/:teamId. Page shows team name as h1, description (if set), Members section listing all team members with usernames and org-level roles, and Projects section listing all attached projects with granted role levels. Loading state shows 'Loading…' spinner. Team-not-found state shows 'Team not found.' message. When no members/projects, show empty-state text.
Permissions: View members: viewer(100); add/remove members & assign: project_lead(500); change roles: maintainer/owner(≥600)

UserStory: As an org admin, I want to rename a team and update its description, so that I can keep team metadata current.
ExpectedBehavior: On team detail page, admin sees 'Edit' and 'Delete team' buttons. Clicking 'Edit' replaces the display with inline inputs pre-filled with current name and description. 'Save' button POSTs PATCH to /api/v2/orgs/:orgId/groups/:groupId with name and description. 'Cancel' dismisses edit mode. Non-admins do not see the button.
Notes: Admin-only (maintainer+ required). Defensive PATCH logic: description only included in payload if server returned one OR user typed non-empty value.
Permissions: View members: viewer(100); add/remove members & assign: project_lead(500); change roles: maintainer/owner(≥600)

UserStory: As an org admin, I want to delete a team I no longer need, so that I can clean up obsolete team structure.
ExpectedBehavior: On team detail page, admin clicks 'Delete team' button. An inline confirmation box appears with text 'Delete '[team name]'? This removes the team and all its grants.' and 'Confirm' / 'Cancel' buttons. Clicking 'Confirm' DELETEs /api/v2/orgs/:orgId/groups/:groupId and navigates to /teams. 'Cancel' dismisses the confirmation. Non-admins do not see the button.
Notes: Admin-only (maintainer+ required). Cascade delete removes all team members and project attachments server-side.
Permissions: Lifecycle ops: project_lead(500)+ / owner(700)

UserStory: As an org admin, I want to add org members to a team, so that I can group people for project access.
ExpectedBehavior: On team detail page, admin sees 'Add member' link. Clicking it reveals a combobox (searchable dropdown) pre-populated with available org members not already in team, a 'Add' button, and 'Cancel' button. Typing filters member list. Selecting a member and clicking 'Add' POSTs to /api/v2/orgs/:orgId/groups/:groupId/members with username. Member appears in Members list. If all org members already in team, show 'All org members are already in this team.' message and disable the Add button.
Notes: Admin-only. Combobox filters and searches by username, excluding users already in team. Does not require a role selection at add-to-team time (org-level role applies).
Permissions: Manage members/invites: project_lead(500); role changes: maintainer/owner(≥600); link role capped at contributor(400)

UserStory: As an org admin, I want to remove a member from a team, so that I can adjust team composition without removing them from the org.
ExpectedBehavior: In Members section of team detail page, each member row has a 'Remove' link (red underline). Clicking it DELETEs /api/v2/orgs/:orgId/groups/:groupId/members/:userId and the member disappears from the list immediately. Non-admins do not see the Remove button.
Notes: Admin-only. Removing from team does NOT remove from org or revoke project access via other paths (org/direct).
Permissions: View members: viewer(100); add/remove members & assign: project_lead(500); change roles: maintainer/owner(≥600)

Feature: Change member org-level role within team context
UserStory: As an org owner, I want to change a team member's org-level role, so that I can adjust their permissions across the organization.
ExpectedBehavior: On team detail page, if caller is owner (level 700+), each member row shows a role-picker (Select dropdown) with all 7 role options. Changing role calls handleChangeMemberRole() which POSTs to /api/v2/orgs/:orgId/members with username and new role. If caller is not owner, the role is shown as a locked badge with a '?' help icon; hovering shows tooltip explaining the role and that it can only be changed by an org owner.
Notes: Owner-only for edits (level 700+). Non-owners see read-only role display with help tooltip explaining the lock. The capability is gated by org-level ownership, not team-level.
Permissions: Manage members/invites: project_lead(500); role changes: maintainer/owner(≥600); link role capped at contributor(400)

Feature: Attach project to team with granted role
UserStory: As an org admin, I want to grant a team access to a project at a specific role level, so that all team members inherit that project access together.
ExpectedBehavior: On team detail page, admin sees 'Attach project' link. Clicking it reveals a Projects section select dropdown (filtered to projects not already attached) and a Role dropdown (7 options). Selecting a project and role and clicking 'Attach' POSTs to /api/v2/orgs/:orgId/groups/:groupId/projects with projectId and roleLevel. Project appears in Projects list with granted role. Non-admins do not see the link.
Notes: Admin-only. Role defaults to Viewer (100). Only offers projects the caller has access to (filtered via fetchAccessibleProjects).
Permissions: View members: viewer(100); add/remove members & assign: project_lead(500); change roles: maintainer/owner(≥600)

Feature: Change team's granted role on a project
UserStory: As an org admin, I want to adjust the role level a team has on an attached project, so that I can fine-tune team access permissions.
ExpectedBehavior: In Projects section of team detail page, each project row shows a role-picker (Select dropdown with 6 options; Owner is excluded). Changing role calls handleChangeProjectRole() which PATCHes /api/v2/orgs/:orgId/groups/:groupId/projects/:projectId with new roleLevel. Role updates immediately. Non-admins do not see the dropdown.
Notes: Admin-only. Owner (700) is intentionally excluded from picker; ownership cannot be transferred via UI.
Permissions: Manage members/invites: project_lead(500); role changes: maintainer/owner(≥600); link role capped at contributor(400)

UserStory: As an org admin, I want to remove a team's access to a project, so that I can clean up stale project attachments.
ExpectedBehavior: In Projects section of team detail page, each project row has a 'Detach' link (red underline). Clicking it DELETEs /api/v2/orgs/:orgId/groups/:groupId/projects/:projectId. Project disappears from the list. Non-admins do not see the link.
Notes: Admin-only. Detaching team project access does not affect direct/org/creator paths to that project for individual members.
Permissions: View members: viewer(100); add/remove members & assign: project_lead(500); change roles: maintainer/owner(≥600)

UserStory: As an org admin, I want to see all members of my organization and their roles, so that I can manage org-wide access.
ExpectedBehavior: Navigate to /members page. Shows 'Members' heading with org name in subtitle. Renders a member roster (MembersPanel) listing all org members with usernames, org-level roles (Viewer/Contributor/Project Lead/Maintainer), and source badge. 'Last active X ago' chip shown if lastActiveAt is set. Stale members (>30 days) get amber highlight. When loading, show 'Loading members…' spinner. When error, show error text with red background. When no org selected, show 'Select an organization' prompt.
Notes: Rendered within MembersShell (AppShell + OrgSidebar). Org role picker excludes Commenter (200) and Reviewer (300) — org-wide comment-only is not surfaced at org level. Last-active tracking depends on migration 0018 landing; null timestamps render no hint.
Permissions: View members: viewer(100); add/remove members & assign: project_lead(500); change roles: maintainer/owner(≥600)

UserStory: As an org admin, I want to add an existing Aquilla user to my organization, so that they can access all org projects at their assigned role.
ExpectedBehavior: On /members page, MembersPanel shows an 'Add' row at bottom with a username typeahead input, role dropdown (Viewer/Contributor/Project Lead/Maintainer default), and 'Add' button. Typing in typeahead searches across all Aquilla users (scopedSearch=false). Selecting username and role and clicking 'Add' calls onAdd() which POSTs to /api/v2/orgs/:orgId/members. If username not found, error message 'Could not add user. Username may not exist.' displays. Member appears in list on success.
Notes: Requires caller to have org membership (useOrgMembers hook implicitly filters). Typeahead excludes already-added members. Default role is MAINTAINER (600) for org context.
Permissions: View members: viewer(100); add/remove members & assign: project_lead(500); change roles: maintainer/owner(≥600)

UserStory: As an org owner, I want to change a member's org-level role, so that I can adjust their permissions without removing them.
ExpectedBehavior: On /members page, each member row shows a role-picker (Select dropdown). Changing role calls onChangeRole() which POSTs to /api/v2/orgs/:orgId/members with username and new role. Role updates on the row. Role picker is only enabled for non-locked members and non-self rows. Locked members (org owner source) show read-only badge without picker.
Notes: Caller can only grant roles up to their own level (callerMaxRole cap). Owner (700) is not shown in picker for org context (only at direct-project level).
Permissions: Manage members/invites: project_lead(500); role changes: maintainer/owner(≥600); link role capped at contributor(400)

UserStory: As an org admin, I want to remove a member from my organization, so that they lose org-wide access and I can clean up inactive users.
ExpectedBehavior: On /members page, each member row has a trash icon button. Clicking it opens a confirmation dialog (RemoveOrgMemberDialog) showing 'Remove [username] from [orgName]?' with warning that they lose org-wide access but keep per-project direct grants. Dialog lists all projects where member has direct grants with checkboxes (default unchecked). User can opt-in to remove from specific projects. 'Remove from org' (or 'Remove from org and N projects' if checked) button confirms. Clicking removes from org and (optionally) from selected projects. Non-owners cannot remove self.
Notes: Caller can only remove members with role <= their own level. Removing from org does not cascade-remove from projects; dialog allows selective per-project removal. Org removal is atomic; project removals are per-project (partial failures still remove org membership).
Permissions: View members: viewer(100); add/remove members & assign: project_lead(500); change roles: maintainer/owner(≥600)

Feature: View per-member project access breakdown (MemberAccessRow expansion)
UserStory: As an org manager, I want to drill down on a member to see all their project access paths (direct/team/org/creator) and resolved effective roles, so that I can understand and manage their complete access picture (AD-12 max-wins).
ExpectedBehavior: On /members page below the main roster, a 'Project access' section shows each member as an expandable row (chevron icon + username). Clicking expands to show: org-level role applicability note, then per-project rows. Each project row displays: project name, resolved effective role (the max), and chips for each contributing path (e.g., 'direct: contributor', 'team Translators: reviewer', 'org: viewer', 'creator'). Direct grants have a 'Revoke direct grant' button. Non-removable paths (team/org/creator) show pointer text 'Also via … — manage in Teams / Members.' Lazy-loading: expansion fetches via GET /api/v2/orgs/:orgId/members/:userId/access when row is first expanded.
Notes: Shows only members with explicit project-level access; members with org-role-only show 'org-role only; no project overrides' summary. Revoke-direct updates immediately via re-fetch. Non-revocable paths point user to Teams/Members for management.
Permissions: View members: viewer(100); add/remove members & assign: project_lead(500); change roles: maintainer/owner(≥600)

Feature: Invite org members to specific projects (multi-project invite dialog)
UserStory: As an operational PM, I want to add an existing org member to multiple projects in one flow without granting org-wide access, so that I can quickly onboard contributors to the projects they need.
ExpectedBehavior: On /members page, 'Add to projects' button (UsersRound icon) opens MultiProjectInviteDialog. Dialog has username typeahead (existing Aquilla user), multi-select checkboxes for projects, and per-project role pickers (default Contributor). Submitting POSTs to /api/v2/projects/:projectId/members for each selected project with username and role. Success shows 'Invite complete' or per-project statuses. Email mode shows explanation that per-project invite links are available in Share panels instead of direct add.
Notes: Button disabled if no accessible projects. Allows granular per-project role selection at invite time. Email mode acknowledges per-project email invites are separate (not directly invitable in bulk).
Permissions: Manage members/invites: project_lead(500); role changes: maintainer/owner(≥600); link role capped at contributor(400)

Feature: View and revoke pending invitations (targeted email + open link)
UserStory: As an org owner, I want to see all outstanding share-link invitations to my projects and revoke them if they're no longer needed, so that I can manage access hygiene.
ExpectedBehavior: On /members page, 'Pending invitations' section (owner-only, gated server-side via 403) lists all unredeemed project invites across the org. Each row shows: project name, role (capitalized), email badge (if targeted) or 'open link' badge, creator username, expiry label (e.g., 'expires in 2 days', 'expired', 'no expiry'), and trash icon. Clicking trash DELETEs /projects/:projectId/invites/:token. Row disappears optimistically; if server errors, re-fetch restores it. Non-owners see no section.
Notes: Section hidden if no pending invites or caller is not owner. Expiry labels computed client-side: 'expired' for past dates, 'expires in N days/hours/minutes' for future. Optimistic revoke means row vanishes immediately even if network fails.
Permissions: Manage members/invites: project_lead(500); role changes: maintainer/owner(≥600); link role capped at contributor(400)

Feature: View external collaborators (non-org members with project access)
UserStory: As a maintainer+ org admin, I want to see all non-members who have access to org projects (via invite links, direct adds, or teams), so that I can govern external access.
ExpectedBehavior: On /members page, 'External collaborators' section (maintainer+ only, AQU-326) lists everyone accessing org projects who is NOT an org member. Each row shows: username, 'external' badge (amber), list of projects they access, and per-project inline 'Revoke' buttons. Clicking revoke DELETEs /projects/:projectId/members/:userId. Section hidden if no externals. Derived on read from members-matrix; not a stored org_members variant.
Notes: Maintainer+ only (level 600+). Derived from members-matrix, not a backend table. Revoking removes direct grant only; doesn't auto-remove from org or teams.
Permissions: Manage members/invites: project_lead(500); role changes: maintainer/owner(≥600); link role capped at contributor(400)

Feature: View per-project members with role sources and secondary paths
UserStory: As a project admin, I want to see everyone with access to a project and their effective role, including where their access comes from (org/team/direct/creator), so that I can manage project membership.
ExpectedBehavior: Navigate to /project/:projectId/members. Renders MembersTab in a two-tab interface (Members / Invite link). Current members list shows each person with: username, source badge ('via org' / 'via team' / 'creator' / none for direct override), role (capability name + level), secondary sources list (e.g., '+ team:reviewer, org:contributor'). Members are sorted and grouped; loading state shows 'Loading members…'. Empty state shows 'No members yet.'
Notes: Nested under ProjectWorkspace via route /project/:id/members. Lists effective members (GET /api/v2/projects/:id/members) with AD-12 max-wins resolution and secondary-source listing.
Permissions: Manage members/invites: project_lead(500); role changes: maintainer/owner(≥600); link role capped at contributor(400)

UserStory: As a project maintainer, I want to add an existing Aquilla user directly to a project, so that I can grant them access without org membership.
ExpectedBehavior: On project members page, 'Add member' section shows username input, role dropdown (Viewer to Maintainer, max-capped by caller), and 'Add' button. Typing username searches/validates. Clicking 'Add' POSTs to /api/v2/projects/:projectId/members with username and role. Submitting shows 'Adding…' state. On success, member appears in the list. On error, shows 'No user found with that username' or server error.
Notes: Caller capped to MAINTAINER (600) max. Input validates on blur/submission. Enter key triggers add.
