Permissions: Run/view checks: contributor(400); author & manage rules / algorithmic-check overrides: project_lead(500)

UserStory: As a translator, I want to catch leading/trailing spaces and double spaces, so that formatting is clean.
ExpectedBehavior: Builtin check 'double-space' runs on cells. If target has leading/trailing whitespace or multiple consecutive spaces, violation is raised. Severity: minor, enabled by default.
Notes: runsOnEmptyTarget=false. Detects multiple spaces and edge whitespace.
Permissions: Run/view checks: contributor(400); author & manage rules / algorithmic-check overrides: project_lead(500)

UserStory: As a translator, I want to catch accidental word repetition in translations, so that typos are prevented.
ExpectedBehavior: Builtin check 'repeated-word' runs on cells. If the same word appears twice consecutively in target (unless source also has the repetition), violation is raised. Severity: minor, enabled by default.
Notes: runsOnEmptyTarget=false. Allows repetition if source also has it.
Permissions: Run/view checks: contributor(400); author & manage rules / algorithmic-check overrides: project_lead(500)

UserStory: As a translator, I want to detect mismatched brackets, parentheses, and braces, so that markup is not corrupted.
ExpectedBehavior: Builtin check 'unpaired-symbols' runs on cells. Counts (, [, { in source/target and checks target has equal counts. Mismatched delimiters raise violation. Severity: minor, enabled by default.
Notes: runsOnEmptyTarget=false. Detects (), [], {} imbalance.
Permissions: Run/view checks: contributor(400); author & manage rules / algorithmic-check overrides: project_lead(500)

UserStory: As a translator, I want to catch when abbreviations change between source and target, so that acronyms and short forms are consistent.
ExpectedBehavior: Builtin check 'abbreviation-mismatch' runs on cells. Extracts abbreviations (sequences of capitals) from source and checks target contains same abbreviations. Missing abbreviations raise violation. Severity: minor, enabled by default.
Notes: runsOnEmptyTarget=false. Detects capital abbreviations like USA, LLM, API.
Permissions: Run/view checks: contributor(400); author & manage rules / algorithmic-check overrides: project_lead(500)

UserStory: As a translator or reviewer, I want to mark a translated cell as validated, so that I can indicate the translation quality meets project standards.
ExpectedBehavior: User clicks the validation button on a cell with non-empty translation → `emitCellValidate` event fires → cell status changes from 'unvalidated' to 'validated' → validation button updates to show emerald indicator and 'Validated' state → cell appears in 'Recent Examples' on memory page.
Notes: Validation is role-gated (requires TRANSLATOR or REVIEWER role minimum); first-validate fires a once-per-session FIRST_CELL_VALIDATE analytics event.
Permissions: Validate/unvalidate: reviewer(300)

UserStory: As a translator or reviewer, I want to remove my validation from a cell, so that I can undo an accidental validation or change my quality assessment.
ExpectedBehavior: User opens validation popover on a self-validated cell → clicks 'Remove your validation' trash button → `emitCellUnvalidate` event fires → cell status changes from 'validated' to 'unvalidated' → button state flips back to unvalidated indicator → user is no longer listed in activeValidators.
Notes: Only available to the user who performed the validation; other validators' validations remain visible and unchanged.
Permissions: Validate/unvalidate: reviewer(300)

UserStory: As a translator, I want to validate multiple cells at once via selection checkboxes, so that I can quickly mark a batch of translations as complete.
ExpectedBehavior: User selects 1+ cells via checkbox → SelectionBar appears with 'Validate N' button → user clicks button → `emitCellValidate` emitted for each selected unvalidated cell → success toast shows count validated → cells update to validated state.
Notes: Skips cells already validated by current user; button disabled if all selected cells are already validated.
Permissions: Validate/unvalidate: reviewer(300)

UserStory: As a translator, I want to remove my validations from multiple cells at once, so that I can quickly undo a batch validation.
ExpectedBehavior: User selects 1+ self-validated cells → SelectionBar shows 'Remove my validations' button → user clicks → `emitCellUnvalidate` emitted for each selected validated cell → button becomes disabled or hidden → success indicated.
Notes: Only removes current user's validations; other validators remain unaffected.
Permissions: Validate/unvalidate: reviewer(300)

UserStory: As a translator, I want to see who has validated each cell and when, so that I can understand the state of collaborative validation.
ExpectedBehavior: User hovers over or clicks validation button on a cell validated by others → validation popover opens → 'Validated by' list shows all active validators with timestamps → if current user validated it, a trash icon appears next to their name for removal.
Notes: Validation history also shown in popover when available (prior validations/unvalidations over time).
Permissions: Validate/unvalidate cells: reviewer(300); health/confidence is derived-on-read (no role to view)

UserStory: As a project manager, I want to see cell health derived from endorsement count and validation proximity, so that I can identify which cells need attention based on context validation.
ExpectedBehavior: For each cell: health = (1 - decay) * 100, where decay = max(0, 1 - endorsementCount / endorsementTarget). Validated cells (endorsementCount >= required) reach 100. Untranslated cells (empty status) have health 0. Health interpolates smoothly between 0-100 based on distance from validation gate.
Notes: Default endorsementTarget is requiredValidations (from project settings, default 1). Explicit decaySettings.endorsementTarget can override per-project tuning.
Permissions: Validate/unvalidate cells: reviewer(300); health/confidence is derived-on-read (no role to view)

UserStory: As a translator, I want to see overall file health, so that I can gauge progress on a particular file.
ExpectedBehavior: File health = mean(decay across all cells in file) converted to 0-100 scale. Updated incrementally as cells are validated. Shown as percentage in sidebar file list (two progress bars: amber for translated%, green for validated%).
Notes: Displayed via two horizontal progress bars in FileRow: first bar shows % translated, second shows % validated.
Permissions: Validate/unvalidate cells: reviewer(300); health/confidence is derived-on-read (no role to view)

UserStory: As a project manager, I want to see overall project health, so that I can track translation completion quality across all files.
ExpectedBehavior: Project health = mean(decay across all cells in all files) converted to 0-100 scale. Displayed as colored HealthRing (red 0-33, amber 34-66, green 67-100) in StatusBar footer and ProjectCard. Updated as files load and cells are validated.
Notes: Endorsement-count path: endorsementCount projects from server validator list or local-only counts. Falls back to 0 on fresh import.
Permissions: Validate/unvalidate cells: reviewer(300); health/confidence is derived-on-read (no role to view)

UserStory: As a project manager, I want project health to reflect server-computed confidence scores from the example-retrieval graph, so that health reflects semantic similarity to validated cells rather than just endorsement counts.
ExpectedBehavior: When serverRollup option is provided to useHealth with projectHealth and fileHealth maps, those values override the endorsement-count path for file/project aggregates. Per-cell healthMap still derives from endorsement or per-cell confidence (via useCellConfidence overlay). Falls back to endorsement-count path if serverRollup is null.
Notes: AD-14 amendment 2026-06-04; per-cell health still uses endorsement-count or confidence overlay (useCellConfidence), not server rollup.
Permissions: Validate/unvalidate cells: reviewer(300); health/confidence is derived-on-read (no role to view)

UserStory: As a translator, I want per-cell health to reflect semantic similarity to validated examples, so that I know which unvalidated cells are most likely ready to validate based on learned patterns.
ExpectedBehavior: useCellConfidence queries sync-worker /cell-confidence endpoint with cellIds and returns confidence scores 0-1 for each cell. Scores converted to health 0-100 and merged into healthMap. Validated cells immediately snap to 100; server ripple adjusts neighbors based on perHopDecay and maxHops settings. Optional overlay toggled via localStorage.
Notes: PROTOTYPE status (AD-14 health-as-confidence). Disabled by default; enabled only via localStorage.setItem('health-confidence-overlay','1'). Runs alongside endorsement path; nothing removed.
Permissions: Validate/unvalidate: reviewer(300)

UserStory: As a translator, I want cells that lack sufficient surrounding validation context to be visually highlighted, so that I can prioritize validating cells in semantic neighborhoods.
ExpectedBehavior: For each cell: if decay > decayWarnThreshold (default 0.66), the cell shows 'needs attention' marker in UI (text in expansion panel or inline visual cue). Absence of marker is silence, not endorsement. Marker appears in cell expansion Staleness tab as text 'Needs attention — nearby context cells haven't been validated yet.'
Notes: Uses server-derived confidence when available, falls back to endorsement-count decay. Threshold tunable per-project (decayWarnThreshold in DecaySettings).
Permissions: Validate/unvalidate cells: reviewer(300); health/confidence is derived-on-read (no role to view)

UserStory: As a user, I want to see health as a colored circular progress indicator, so that I can quickly gauge validation state at a glance.
ExpectedBehavior: HealthRing component renders circular SVG arc proportional to health (0-100). Color: red (0-33), amber (34-66), green (67-100). At health=0, ring hidden but container occupies space (no layout shift). Used on cell rows (size 22px) and ProjectCard (size 22px) and StatusBar (size 18px).
Notes: Can render an icon inside the ring (e.g., cell endorsement count or project health %). Smooth 0.5s transitions on health/color changes.
Permissions: Validate/unvalidate cells: reviewer(300); health/confidence is derived-on-read (no role to view)

UserStory: As a project manager, I want to understand which cells are dragging down project health, so that I can focus validation efforts on high-impact areas.
ExpectedBehavior: User hovers over health ring (StatusBar or ProjectCard) → popover opens showing: overall health%, percentage of cells needing attention, list of 'biggest drags' (8 cells with lowest health, sorted ascending). Optional stale-source count displayed. Clicking a drag cell jumps to it in editor.
Notes: Uses attentionHealthCutoff = (1 - warnThreshold)*100 to filter cells needing attention. Shows 'No cells need attention' when list is empty.
Permissions: Validate/unvalidate cells: reviewer(300); health/confidence is derived-on-read (no role to view)

UserStory: As a project manager, I want to see project health on the dashboard without opening the project, so that I can quickly compare health across many projects.
ExpectedBehavior: ProjectCard displays a HealthRing with server-fetched projectHealth (via useProjectHealth). Ring hidden if projectHealth is null (local-only project or fetch error). Health fetched from sync-worker /health-rollup route using project-scoped sync token.
Notes: AQU-190: token fetcher cached module-level per projectId to avoid N+1 stampede. Falls back gracefully if project not yet server-side (local-only).
Permissions: Validate/unvalidate cells: reviewer(300); health/confidence is derived-on-read (no role to view)

Feature: File progress tracking (translated and validated counts)
UserStory: As a translator, I want to see how many cells in each file are translated and validated, so that I can monitor work completion.
ExpectedBehavior: useHealth.fileProgress Map tracks {translated, validated, total} per file. Derived from cell.status: 'translated' = not empty, 'validated' = status=='validated'. Displayed in FileRow as two inline progress bars (amber for translated%, green for validated%). Tooltip shows exact counts.
Notes: Updated incrementally; memo held via structural-stability helpers so non-progress typing doesn't re-render rows.
Permissions: Validate/unvalidate cells: reviewer(300); health/confidence is derived-on-read (no role to view)

UserStory: As a translator, I want to see total counts of cells and validation state at a glance, so that I can quickly gauge overall progress.
ExpectedBehavior: StatusBar footer displays: total cells, translated count & %, unvalidated count (if > 0, shown in amber pill), validated count (if > 0, shown in green pill). Clickable health ring opens decay breakdown popover.
Notes: Uses healthMap per-cell values and file progress aggregates. Placed at bottom of editor viewport.
Permissions: Validate/unvalidate: reviewer(300)

UserStory: As a translator, I want to see which cells have open discussion threads, so that I can prioritize addressing feedback.
ExpectedBehavior: useHealth.cellOpenCommentCount tracks count of open (unresolved) threads per cellId. EditorTable renders comment icon with badge showing count when > 0. Clicking icon opens comments panel. Cell expansion shows count in tooltip.
Notes: Derived from cell.threads filter(status == 'open'). Used to badge cell rows and CommentTab.
Permissions: Validate/unvalidate cells: reviewer(300); health/confidence is derived-on-read (no role to view)

UserStory: As a project manager, I want to see how many open comments exist across the project, so that I can gauge discussion volume.
ExpectedBehavior: useHealth.projectOpenCommentCount is sum of openCommentCount across all files. Displayed as badge on Comments nav link / tab. Used to route users to pending discussions.
Notes: Only counts open (unresolved) threads; closed/resolved threads excluded.
Permissions: Validate/unvalidate cells: reviewer(300); health/confidence is derived-on-read (no role to view)

UserStory: As a QA manager, I want QA rule violations to be flagged separately from health, so that rule violations don't conflate with validation-based confidence.
ExpectedBehavior: useHealth.infractions is Map<cellId, RuleInfraction[]>. Populated by checkRulesForCell for enabled rules. Incremental: cached per cell signature (status, original, translated); only re-run on actual content change, not every keystroke. Infractions shown in cell expansion Issues tab.
Notes: AD-14: infractions carried as sibling surface, NOT folded into health (health only uses decay/endorsement/confidence).
Permissions: Validate/unvalidate cells: reviewer(300); health/confidence is derived-on-read (no role to view)

UserStory: As a translator, I want to dismiss a QA rule violation with an optional justification, so that I can suppress false positives and explain intentional violations.
ExpectedBehavior: User clicks infraction in Issues tab → ViolationPopover opens → clicks 'Waive' → optional reason input appears → 'Confirm' → `emitCellWaive` fires with ruleId and reason → popover closes → infraction moves to 'Waived' subsection showing waive details (reason, username, timestamp).
Notes: Waiver is keyed on (cell, ruleId). Can be revoked with 'Unwaive' button showing same popover in reverse.
Permissions: Validate/unvalidate cells: reviewer(300); health/confidence is derived-on-read (no role to view)

UserStory: As a translator, I want to restore a waived rule violation, so that I can reevaluate or remove a prior dismissal.
ExpectedBehavior: User clicks waived infraction in 'Waived' subsection → ViolationPopover opens showing waive details → 'Unwaive' button → click → `emitCellUnwaive` fires → popover closes → infraction moves back to active Issues list.
Notes: Reverses a prior waiver without requiring reason.
Permissions: Validate/unvalidate cells: reviewer(300); health/confidence is derived-on-read (no role to view)

Feature: Decay settings configuration (maxHops and attention threshold)
UserStory: As a project manager, I want to tune how far validated cells' confidence ripples and at what point cells are flagged as needing attention, so that I can customize health scoring to project context.
ExpectedBehavior: ProjectSettings > Staleness & health section shows: 'Max hops' input (1-20, default 4) controlling propagation radius in confidence graph, and 'Attention threshold' input (0-1, default 0.66) controlling when 'needs attention' marker appears. Changes saved to project.decaySettings.
Notes: maxHops passed to both useHealthRollup (server path) and useCellConfidence (confidence overlay). retired endorsementTarget no longer shown; confidence derived on read, not from endorsement writes.
Permissions: Validate/unvalidate cells: reviewer(300); health/confidence is derived-on-read (no role to view)

Feature: Living memory validated cell recent examples
UserStory: As a translator, I want to see recently validated cells as reference examples, so that I can learn from team translations and maintain consistency.
ExpectedBehavior: Memory page > Recent Examples section displays ValidatedCellCard for each validated cell (status == 'validated') across all project files. Each card shows source text (aria-label='Source text') and translation (aria-label='Translation'). Sorted by most recent validation.
Notes: useLivingMemory hook filters cells for status === 'validated'. ValidatedCellCard component renders with labeled sections.
Permissions: Source content edits: project_lead(500)

UserStory: As a translator, I want to see when the source text has changed since I last translated a cell, so that I can identify cells needing re-translation.
ExpectedBehavior: StaleSourceIndicator component shows amber triangle icon (AlertTriangle) with tooltip 'The source has changed since this translation was last revised.' when cell's source event_id differs from target row's staleness pin. Icon appears in cell action rail. Managed mode: parent passes staleCellIds Set; standalone mode: hook fetches internally.
Notes: Component exported but NOT yet wired into EditorTable (Phase 5 scope; 2c-β editor rewrite will integrate). Two consumption modes: parent-managed (preferred for row rendering) or standalone.
Permissions: Source content edits: project_lead(500)

UserStory: As a translator, I want to post a comment on a specific cell, so that I can ask questions or provide feedback about that cell's translation.
ExpectedBehavior: User hovers over a cell row in the editor, clicks the 'Add comment' button, types text in the CommentsDrawer textarea, and clicks 'Post'. The comment appears immediately in the drawer (optimistic), and is persisted to the server via comment.create event.
Notes: Cell-scoped comments are enqueued with the cell's fileId. Comments are stored per cell (cellId) and file (fileId).
Permissions: Comment create/edit/delete/resolve: commenter(200)

UserStory: As a translator, I want to submit a comment by pressing Ctrl+Enter (or Cmd+Enter on Mac), so that I can quickly post without using the mouse.
ExpectedBehavior: User types text in the comment textarea and presses Ctrl+Enter (or Cmd+Enter). The comment is submitted and the textarea clears.
Notes: Works in both the cell-scoped CommentsDrawer and the CommentsPage reply composer.
Permissions: Any authenticated user — scoped to own account

UserStory: As a translator, I want to see all comments posted on a cell organized as a thread, so that I can understand the full conversation context.
ExpectedBehavior: When CommentsDrawer opens for a cell, all comments (root + replies) are displayed in order. Each comment shows author, timestamp, and body text (with markdown formatting: **bold**, *italic*, `code`, @mentions). Resolved threads show a 'resolved' badge.
Notes: Deleted comments render as '[deleted]' placeholder (soft-delete model: deletedAt is set but record remains).
Permissions: Comment create/edit/delete/resolve: commenter(200)

UserStory: As a translator, I want to reply to an existing comment, so that I can engage in a conversation about a specific cell.
ExpectedBehavior: User opens the CommentsDrawer and sees the root comment. Below it is a 'Reply...' textarea and a 'Reply' button (disabled until text is entered). Typing text and clicking 'Reply' posts the reply (parentCommentId set to root comment's ID) and clears the textarea.
Notes: Replies are only enabled in the editor drawer (CommentsPage shows a 'not yet wired' message for replies).
Permissions: Comment create/edit/delete/resolve: commenter(200)

UserStory: As a translator, I want to post a reply AND resolve the thread in a single action, so that I can provide a solution and mark the issue as closed.
ExpectedBehavior: User fills the reply textarea and clicks 'Close with reply'. Both the reply is posted (with parentCommentId) AND the thread is marked resolved in one action. The reply text appears in the thread, and the Resolve button is replaced with Reopen.
Notes: The 'Close with reply' button only appears when both canReply and canResolve are true (based on permissions).
Permissions: Comment create/edit/delete/resolve: commenter(200)

UserStory: As a translator or reviewer, I want to mark a comment thread as resolved, so that I can indicate that the issue has been addressed.
ExpectedBehavior: User clicks the 'Resolve' button on a thread. The thread immediately shows resolved state (badge, opacity change), and the button changes to 'Reopen'. The resolved flag is persisted via comment.resolve event.
Notes: Resolved threads are collapsed by default in CommentsPage. The resolver's username is captured as author on the resolve event.
Permissions: Comment create/edit/delete/resolve: commenter(200)

UserStory: As a translator, I want to reopen a resolved thread, so that I can re-engage with the conversation if needed.
ExpectedBehavior: User clicks 'Reopen' on a resolved thread. The thread returns to open state (badge removed, opacity reset) and the button changes back to 'Resolve'. The change is persisted via comment.resolve event with resolved=false.
Notes: Reopening is the inverse of resolving; both use the same resolveThread API with a boolean flag.
Permissions: Comment create/edit/delete/resolve: commenter(200)

UserStory: As a translator, I want to edit a comment I posted, so that I can correct typos or clarify my message.
ExpectedBehavior: User hovers over their own comment (in CommentsPage) and clicks the 'Edit' button in the kebab menu. An inline textarea appears with the current body. User types new text and clicks 'Save' (or presses Cmd/Ctrl+Enter), or 'Cancel' to discard. The edit is persisted via comment.edit event.
Notes: Edit is only available in CommentsPage (not in the cell-scoped drawer). Only the comment author can edit their own comment (authorId === currentUsername check). Soft-deleted comments cannot be edited.
Permissions: Comment create/edit/delete/resolve: commenter(200)

UserStory: As a translator, I want to delete a comment I posted, so that I can remove comments I no longer want visible.
ExpectedBehavior: User hovers over their own comment (in CommentsPage) and clicks the 'Delete' button in the kebab menu. A confirmation dialog appears ('Delete comment? This action cannot be undone.'). User clicks 'Delete' to confirm or 'Cancel' to dismiss. The comment is soft-deleted (body cleared, deletedAt set) via comment.delete event.
Notes: Deletion is soft-delete: the comment record remains in the database with deletedAt timestamp, and body is cleared. Deleted comments display '[deleted]' placeholder. Only the comment author can delete their own comment.
Permissions: Comment create/edit/delete/resolve: commenter(200)

UserStory: As a project manager or reviewer, I want to view all comments across the entire project, so that I can get a holistic view of feedback and issues.
ExpectedBehavior: User navigates to /project/:id/comments. The page loads and displays all project-level, file-level, and cell-level comments grouped by thread. Comments are fetched via useComments hook (project-wide scope, no fileId/cellId filter). A header shows the total comment count.
Notes: The page renders a 'No comments yet' empty state when the project has no comments. Comments are grouped by root+replies, not flattened.
Permissions: Comment create/edit/delete/resolve: commenter(200)

UserStory: As a user, I want to search comments by keyword, so that I can find relevant comments quickly.
ExpectedBehavior: User opens CommentsPage, types in the 'Search comments…' input. Threads matching the search term (case-insensitive substring in root body or any reply body) remain visible; non-matching threads are hidden. An active filter badge shows '1 filter'. Clearing the search restores all threads.
Notes: Search is client-side substring matching (not FTS). The search includes both root and reply bodies.
Permissions: Comment create/edit/delete/resolve: commenter(200)

UserStory: As a reviewer, I want to filter comments by file, so that I can focus on feedback for a specific file.
ExpectedBehavior: User clicks 'Filters' to expand the filter panel. A 'File' select dropdown appears with options 'All files' + list of files that have comments. Selecting a file filters to show only threads from that file.
Notes: File filter dropdown only appears if there are multiple files with comments. Deleted files are shown as 'Deleted file' tombstone entries.
Permissions: Comment create/edit/delete/resolve: commenter(200)

UserStory: As a reviewer, I want to filter comments by the person who posted them, so that I can focus on feedback from a specific team member.
ExpectedBehavior: User clicks 'Filters' to expand the filter panel. An 'Author' select dropdown appears with options 'Anyone' + list of users who have posted root comments. Selecting an author filters to show only threads where the root comment author matches.
Notes: Author filter matches only the root comment author, not reply authors.
Permissions: Comment create/edit/delete/resolve: commenter(200)

UserStory: As a reviewer, I want to see all threads where a specific person participated (either as root author or replier), so that I can track conversations involving that person.
ExpectedBehavior: User clicks 'Filters' to expand the filter panel. A 'Participant' select dropdown appears with options 'Anyone' + list of users who have posted comments or replies. Selecting a participant filters to show only threads where that user is either the root author OR replied.
Notes: Participant filter checks both root author and all reply authors, unlike Author filter which only checks root.
Permissions: Comment create/edit/delete/resolve: commenter(200)

UserStory: As a reviewer, I want to toggle visibility of resolved threads, so that I can focus on open issues or review completed discussions.
ExpectedBehavior: User clicks 'Filters' to expand the filter panel. A 'Show resolved' checkbox appears, unchecked by default. Checking it shows resolved threads (in collapsed state); unchecking hides them. The badge count is unaffected but thread visibility changes immediately.
Notes: Resolved threads are collapsed by default (useState(!root.resolved)). The checkbox is part of the expanded filters panel.
Permissions: Comment create/edit/delete/resolve: commenter(200)

UserStory: As a reviewer, I want to change the sort order of comments, so that I can see the most relevant threads first.
ExpectedBehavior: User clicks 'Filters' to expand the filter panel. A 'Sort' select dropdown appears with options: 'Unresolved first' (default, unresolved threads first then by createdAt DESC), 'Most recent activity' (by updatedAt DESC), 'Newest first' (by createdAt DESC). Selecting an option re-sorts threads immediately.
Notes: The 'unresolved-first' sort is a composite sort: unresolved threads first (boolean check), then by createdAt descending among each group.
Permissions: Comment create/edit/delete/resolve: commenter(200)

UserStory: As a user, I want to expand or collapse the filter controls, so that I can focus on the comments list when not filtering.
ExpectedBehavior: User clicks the 'Filters' button (with SlidersHorizontal icon). The filter panel expands to show Sort, Show resolved, File, Author, Participant, and Reset controls. Clicking 'Filters' again collapses the panel.
Notes: The filter panel is initially collapsed. The search box is always visible (not part of the collapsible section).
Permissions: Comment create/edit/delete/resolve: commenter(200)

UserStory: As a user, I want to quickly clear all active filters, so that I can return to viewing all comments.
ExpectedBehavior: User clicks 'Filters' to expand the filter panel. A 'Reset' button appears at the bottom of the panel. Clicking it clears all filters (search, fileId, authorId, participant, showResolved) and resets sort to default ('unresolved-first').
Notes: The Reset button calls onChange(DEFAULT_FILTER), which resets to: search='', fileId='', authorId='', participant='', showResolved=false, sort='unresolved-first'.
Permissions: Comment create/edit/delete/resolve: commenter(200)

UserStory: As a user, I want to manually refresh the comments list, so that I can see new comments from other users without waiting for automatic updates.
ExpectedBehavior: User clicks the 'Refresh' button (outline, sm, in the page header). The button shows a spinner while loading and is disabled. Comments are re-fetched from the server. After fetch completes, the button returns to normal state showing 'Refresh' text.
Notes: The refresh endpoint is fetchCommentsForProject (sync-worker read API), not a live subscription. Optimistic comments are preserved during refresh via mergeWithOptimistic.
Permissions: Comment create/edit/delete/resolve: commenter(200)

UserStory: As a reviewer, I want to navigate from the CommentsPage to the actual cell in the editor, so that I can see the cell context and respond inline.
ExpectedBehavior: On CommentsPage, for each cell-scoped comment thread, an 'Open file' button appears with an 'Go to cell in editor' tooltip. Clicking it navigates to /project/:id/file/:fileId?cellId=:cellId, opening the file in the editor and scrolling to the relevant cell.
Notes: The button is disabled if the file has been deleted (tombstone state). Project-level and file-level comments do not have an 'Open file' button.
Permissions: Comment create/edit/delete/resolve: commenter(200)

UserStory: As a user, I want to navigate back to the project workspace from the Comments page, so that I can resume editing.
ExpectedBehavior: Comments lives inside the workspace shell. There is no page-level 'Back to project' button — return via the breadcrumb, history arrows, or by selecting a file in the sidebar (navigates to /project/:id/editor/file/:fileId).
Notes: Shell owns navigation (same contract as Living Memory and Rules).
Permissions: Comment create/edit/delete/resolve: commenter(200)

UserStory: As a reviewer, I want to see when a cell's translation has changed since a comment was created, so that I know to re-evaluate the comment's relevance.
ExpectedBehavior: In the cell-scoped CommentsDrawer, if a comment was created when the cell had an empty translation (createdForTranslated=''), and the cell now has a non-empty translation (currentTranslated !== ''), an amber 'stale' indicator with AlertTriangle icon appears next to the thread status badge. Tooltip says 'Translation changed since this thread was created'.
Notes: Staleness is computed as thread.createdForTranslated !== currentTranslated. This helps reviewers catch comments that may no longer apply after translation updates.
Permissions: Comment create/edit/delete/resolve: commenter(200)

UserStory: As a user, I want to @mention team members in comments, so that I can notify them about discussions.
ExpectedBehavior: User types '@' in a comment textarea followed by a prefix (e.g., '@al'). A typeahead dropdown appears showing matching users (from useUserSearch). User can click a user to insert '@username' (with trailing space) at the mention position. If less than 2 characters after '@', 'Type more to search…' message appears.
Notes: Mentions are rendered in the comment body as @username. The mention text is not yet used to trigger notifications (feature-gated or not yet implemented).
Permissions: Comment create/edit/delete/resolve: commenter(200)

UserStory: As a user, I want to format comments with markdown, so that I can emphasize important parts and make comments more readable.
ExpectedBehavior:
User types markdown syntax in the comment body: **text** renders as bold , *text* renders as italic , `text` renders as code , newlines render as
, @mentions render as styled spans. HTML is escaped and sanitized (DOMPurify) to prevent injection.
Notes: Rendering is done via renderCommentHtml + DOMPurify sanitization. Only a narrow set of tags are allowed: b, i, code, br, span (for mentions). This prevents XSS while enabling basic formatting.
Permissions: Comment create/edit/delete/resolve: commenter(200)

UserStory: As a project member, I want to see comments posted by other team members, so that I can collaborate on shared feedback.
ExpectedBehavior: When one user posts a comment, another user who is a project member can see it on the CommentsPage after refreshing (or via live sync if implemented). Comments are stored server-side in the D1 comments projection table and served to all project members.
Notes: Comments are server-persisted and visible to all project members. The CommentsPage fetches all project comments on mount (no live subscription currently).
Permissions: Comment create/edit/delete/resolve: commenter(200)

UserStory: As a project member, I want to reply to comments from other team members, so that I can contribute to ongoing discussions.

Candidates are ranked by NC-value (default). A CandidateTermsPanel renders with a list of ranked candidates, each showing: term text, n-gram length badge, frequency count, NC/C/G² scores (with tooltips), and 'Promote to managed' button (disabled if already managed). Mining status shows 'Mining…' spinner while processing.

Notes: Expand/collapse state local to the component (no persistence). Cell preview truncated on small screens.

Feature: Pre-acceptance warning band for forbidden/missing renderings
UserStory: As a translator using AI copilot, I want to see advisory warnings when an AI completion uses a forbidden term or misses an approved term before I accept it, so that I can catch terminology issues early without blocking my work.

Forbidden-present warnings (louder, alert icon, amber bold text): 'Forbidden rendering "[text]" used for [sourceTerm].' Notes: Component implemented; NOT YET MOUNTED in copilot completion path (glue wave TODO: ProjectWorkspace.tsx). Only active concepts evaluated. Matching is wildcard-aware like everywhere else.

Feature: Wildcard matching for inflectional terms (e.g., grace* matches grace/graced/gracia)
UserStory: As a project lead, I want to define a source term with a trailing `*` wildcard to match inflected forms without manually listing each variant, so that I can cover grace, graced, gracia, etc. with one entry.
ExpectedBehavior: User enters 'grac*' in the source term field. The system treats `*` as standing for zero-or-more Unicode letters (\p{L}*). Matching is case-insensitive and word-boundary aware (leading/trailing boundaries apply unless `*` is present). Enforcement, chips, preacceptance warnings, and candidate exclusion all use the same matcher, so grac* consistently matches grace/graced/gracia/gracier/gracious.
Notes: Escapes regex specials (.+*?...) so literal a.b matches only 'a.b', never 'axb'. Wildcard expands to \p{L}* (Unicode letters), not \w (which is ASCII and matches digits/_).
Permissions: Read glossary: viewer(100); confirm/invalidate/edit terms: contributor(400)

UserStory: As a translator, I want to draft all untranslated cells in my current file/selection with AI, so that I can rapidly bootstrap translations for bulk review.

UserStory: As a translator, I want the AI to translate a paragraph as a coherent unit with discourse context, so that pronouns, tense, and connectives flow naturally across sentence boundaries.
ExpectedBehavior: When a paragraph is selected (≥2 cells), the translator can trigger completion. Instead of translating each cell in isolation, the LLM receives: the whole paragraph's source cells (tagged with stable <c id> tags), the committed preceding target context (discourse window left), following source (right), and few-shot examples. The LLM responds with matching <c id> tags; response is parsed back to per-cell text and committed. Missing/extra/duplicate tags surface as errors.
Notes: Encodes cells with <c id="CELLID">TEXT</c>. Parser reconciles response LOUDLY (missing/extra ids reported). Discourse window uses committed TARGET (not source) on left, source-only on right. Validated pairs + retrieved passages are injected first, then discourse context.

UserStory: As a translator, I want to see the LLM response appear word-by-word as it's generated, so that I can read along and stop if it's going wrong.

UI re-renders on each chunk (streaming preview). When stream ends (or stops), the accumulated text is what gets committed/returned. If stream is aborted (user clicks Stop), the AbortController.signal fires, read loop exits, partial text is discarded, and DOMException('AbortError') is thrown.
Notes: consumeStream handles SSE frame buffering (lines may span read() boundaries). onChunk called with accumulated full text (not delta). Abort via signal kills the fetch + loop immediately. Frontier streaming currently disabled (worker SSE bug workaround) for provider='frontier', but custom providers stream normally.

UserStory: As the system, I want to parse streaming LLM responses robustly, so that errors don't crash the translation.
ExpectedBehavior: LLM SSE stream is consumed line-by-line. Lines are buffered across arbitrary read() boundaries so mid-frame breaks don't lose data. Each 'data: {...}' line is JSON-parsed. Content delta extracted to onChunk. If parsing fails, a console.warn logs the bad frame (first 200 chars) and the loop continues. Stream errors (e.g., 'error': '...') are caught + thrown (bubble up to caller as Error). '[DONE]' or done flag ends stream gracefully.
Notes: Both chat and agent use similar stream consumers (completion-service, agent-client). Line buffering handles edge case where SSE frame split across reader.read() boundaries. Unparseable frames trigger console.warn, not throw (resilient).
Permissions: Apply AI proposal target.cell.commit: contributor(400); cell.validate proposal: reviewer(300)

ExpectedBehavior: User clicks 'Orgs' tab. Page loads table with columns: Org name, Owner username, Member count, Project count, Created date. Each org row has an 'Open' button that navigates to that org's overview (platform admin sees owner-level access to all orgs). Table displays empty message if no orgs exist.
Notes: Data from getAdminOrgs() API. Dates formatted via fmtDate helper. The 'Open' button calls openOrg() callback which sets active org context.
Permissions: Platform-admin only (isPlatformAdminUsername allowlist)

UserStory: As a platform admin, I want to see all teams organized by their parent org, so that I can audit group structure across the platform.
ExpectedBehavior: User clicks 'Teams' tab. Teams are grouped by org (order preserved from API). Each org group shows a section header with org name and team count. A table under each section lists: Team (relative path, with leading org stripped), Members count, Projects count, Created date. Empty state shows message if no teams exist.
Notes: Teams pre-sorted by org on the server. groupByOrg() helper handles client-side grouping. Team names are GitLab full_paths; relativeTeamPath() strips the org segment.
Permissions: Platform-admin only (isPlatformAdminUsername allowlist)

UserStory: As a platform admin, I want to see all users with their email, org membership, and activity, so that I can monitor user engagement and access.
ExpectedBehavior: User clicks 'Users' tab. Page displays table with columns: Username (with display name in parentheses if available), Email, Org count, Last active date, Joined date. All dates formatted via fmtDate helper. No pagination visible; all users from getAdminUsers() API are shown.
Notes: Display name falls back to username if not set. Dates show '—' if null.
Permissions: Platform-admin only (isPlatformAdminUsername allowlist)

UserStory: As a platform admin, I want to view all projects with validation progress and status, so that I can see translation completion across tenants.
ExpectedBehavior: User clicks 'Projects' tab. Page displays table with columns: Project name (clickable link to /projects/:id for active projects; plain text for archived), Org name, Creator username, Validation % (cells validated / total cells), Word count (formatted with commas), Status ('Active' or 'Archived'). Archived projects show no link.
Notes: Validation % calculated via pct() helper. Project name links only render for non-archived projects. Org name and creator show '—' if null.
Permissions: Platform-admin only (isPlatformAdminUsername allowlist)

UserStory: As a platform admin, I want to see a global activity feed with user actions and descriptions, so that I can audit what has happened across the platform.
ExpectedBehavior: User clicks 'Activity' tab. Page displays table with columns: When (timestamp), User (username or user ID fallback), Type (event type string), Description (free-text description). Most recent 200 activity records from getAdminActivity(jwt, 200) are shown. All dates formatted via fmtDate.
Notes: Limited to 200 records by server API call. Fallback to #userId if username not available. Type and Description show '—' if null.
Permissions: Platform-admin only (isPlatformAdminUsername allowlist)

UserStory: As a platform admin, I want to see the allowlist of platform admins and their account status, so that I know who has unrestricted access.
ExpectedBehavior: User clicks 'Admins' tab. Page displays explanatory text stating that platform admins are allowlisted in PLATFORM_ADMINS (wrangler.toml) and redeploy is required to change. A table shows: Username (with display name in parentheses), Account status ('Registered' or red 'No account'), Email, Last active date, Joined date. Usernames and emails fallback gracefully if null. Dates show '—' if null.
Notes: No edit UI; this is informational only (editing requires code deploy). getAdminAdmins() API fetches the list. Account status (hasAccount field) is color-coded (green for registered, red text for no account).
Permissions: Platform-admin only (isPlatformAdminUsername allowlist)

UserStory: As a platform admin, I want to monitor and configure per-org credit budgets and spending, so that I can manage cost and prevent runaway agent sessions.
ExpectedBehavior: User clicks 'Compute / Credits' tab. Page loads with explanatory text about credit pricing and cap enforcement. Table displays per-org rows with: Org name, Daily total spend, Daily agent spend (highlighted in amber), Weekly total spend, Weekly agent spend (highlighted), Editable daily cap input, Editable weekly cap input, Enforce toggle (log-only vs hard-blocking), Show to org toggle (reveal panel to org maintainers). Each spend cell shows formatted credit amount + progress bar (color: green/amber/red based on % used). Agent rail is visually emphasized. Caps and toggles are inline-editable; changes save on blur/click. If no orgs, shows 'No orgs found.' message.
Notes: Platform-admin gate enforced by AdminConsole. Server re-enforces on every API call. Agent spend is visually highlighted (amber background) because agent runs are expensive and unpredictable. Markup is 5× for agent rail vs. standard. caps are advisory when enforce=false.
Permissions: Platform-admin only (isPlatformAdminUsername allowlist)

UserStory: As a developer, I want to inspect all local projects and their configuration, so that I can debug project structure and state.
ExpectedBehavior: User navigates to /debug. If no :id param, page calls listProjects() and renders the full project list as JSON in a <pre> block. If :id is provided and path is /settings/debug, calls getProject(id) and renders project + completionSettings + username as JSON. Otherwise calls getProject(id) and renders project + files as JSON. Loading state shows 'Loading...' in pre block until data arrives. Output is always valid JSON.
Notes: Dev-only tool for local debugging. No access control shown in code (likely unrestricted). Routes: /debug, /project/:id/settings/debug, /project/:id/debug.
Permissions: Platform-admin only (isPlatformAdminUsername allowlist); debug shells are dev-gated

UserStory: As a developer or user, I want to see the current app version and build SHA at a glance, so that I know what version I'm running.
ExpectedBehavior: On routes without a left rail (dashboard, onboarding, join, settings, non-workspace pages), a floating badge appears bottom-left showing version and branch/SHA (e.g., 'v0.1.2 · main · abc123def'). Clicking the badge copies full build info to clipboard (title: 'v0.1.2 · main · abc123def\nbuild: main@abc123def'). Badge text changes to 'Copied' with a check icon for 1.5 seconds. Hovering shows tooltip with copy instructions. Badge does not appear on pages with left rail (AppShell sidebar pages) to avoid duplication with VersionTag.
Notes: Build info comes from compile-time globals __APP_VERSION__, __APP_BRANCH__, __APP_SHA__. On production branch (main/production), branch is not shown in label. hasLeftRail() hides badge on full-height workspace pages. Fixed position z-30, bottom-left corner.
Permissions: Platform-admin only (isPlatformAdminUsername allowlist); debug shells are dev-gated

UserStory: As a developer or user, I want to see the current app version in the left sidebar footer, so that I know the running version while working.
ExpectedBehavior: On routes with a left rail (AppShell sidebar, ProjectWorkspace, etc.), a version tag button appears at the foot of the sidebar (mt-auto). Text shows version label (e.g., 'v0.1.2 · main · abc123def'). Clicking copies full build info to clipboard and shows 'Copied' state for 1.5 seconds. Hovering shows tooltip with copy instructions. Text is small (font-mono, text-[10px]), muted color, and truncates on small widths.
Notes: Mount point: (1) AppShell sidebar footer for org pages, (2) LeftDock footer for ProjectWorkspace. Same copy-to-clipboard behavior as floating badge. Colors: muted-foreground/40 base, muted-foreground/70 hover, emerald-600 when copied.
Permissions: Platform-admin only (isPlatformAdminUsername allowlist); debug shells are dev-gated

UserStory: As a user, I want to know when a new app version is available, so that I can refresh to get the latest features and fixes.
ExpectedBehavior: useUpdateCheck() hook polls /version.json every 60 seconds (in production only; skipped in dev). If the server's SHA differs from the current __APP_SHA__, UpdateBanner component appears as a fixed bottom-left button (z-30) showing 'Update available' with a refresh icon. The dot pulse animation draws attention. Clicking the button calls window.location.reload(). Banner is hidden if already running latest version.
Notes: Poll interval: 60s (POLL_MS). Only runs in production (skips if import.meta.env.DEV). Fetch uses cache-busting query param (?_=Date.now()). Banner has slide-in-from-bottom + fade-in animation. Styled with violet accent. Positioned above or below version badge/tag depending on layout.
Permissions: Platform-admin only (isPlatformAdminUsername allowlist); debug shells are dev-gated

UserStory: As a user, I want to easily report bugs or issues without leaving the app, so that I can quickly surface problems I encounter.
ExpectedBehavior: Small flag icon button appears at the foot of the left rail/dock (next to VersionTag). Clicking opens ReportProblemDialog. Button has tooltip 'Report a problem' and is small/unobtrusive (text-muted-foreground/50, hover highlights to muted-foreground/70).
Notes: Mounted in two places: (1) AppShell sidebar footer for org pages, (2) LeftDock footer for workspace. Icon is lucide-react Flag component (h-3 w-3).
Permissions: Platform-admin only (isPlatformAdminUsername allowlist); debug shells are dev-gated

UserStory: As a user, I want to describe what went wrong and have it automatically captured with context, so that the team can investigate my issue.
ExpectedBehavior: Dialog opens with title 'Report a problem' and description explaining consent state. User types free-text description in textarea. Auto-captured context shown: current route, active project ID (if any), active file ID (if any). If analytics enabled, shows 'Send report' button that submits via captureReportProblem() (PostHog event with replay URL if available). If analytics disabled, shows 'Copy report' button (copies plain-text report to clipboard) and amber warning explaining analytics are off. After submission, shows 'Thanks — report received' message with session replay URL if available. Cancel button closes dialog. Dialog resets state on close.
Notes: Consent-aware: relies on isAnalyticsConsent().enabled to determine send vs. copy path. captureReportProblem() returns boolean (true if sent, false if analytics off). getSessionReplayUrl() retrieves PostHog session replay URL if available. buildReportText() formats plain-text version for manual copying. Route params (:id, :fileId) captured via useParams<{ id?: string; fileId?: string }>.
Permissions: Platform-admin only (isPlatformAdminUsername allowlist); debug shells are dev-gated

Feature: Status Bar — Project Health & Cell Progress
UserStory: As a translator, I want to see the overall health of my project and progress at a glance, so that I understand translation completion and quality.
ExpectedBehavior: At the bottom of the workspace, a footer shows: (1) Health ring (0-100 circle indicator; colors: red ≤33, amber 34-66, green ≥67) with health number inside; (2) Decay breakdown popover on hover/click showing 'X% of cells need attention' and top 8 'biggest drags' (cells sorted by descending decay). Stale source count displayed separately if > 0. (3) Summary stats: 'N cells · M translated (P%)' + badge showing unvalidated count (amber) and validated count (green) if > 0.
Notes: StatusBar component receives: cells (CellData array), projectHealth (0-100), healthMap (per-cell decay map), staleSourceCount (optional), onJumpToCell callback. HealthRing shows SVG circle, animated stroke-dashoffset. DecayBreakdown popover opens on hover (delay 300ms, close delay 120ms). Biggest drags clickable to jump to cell if callback provided.
Permissions: Validate/unvalidate: reviewer(300)

UserStory: As a user, I want a compact visual indicator of health/decay status, so that I can quickly assess quality at a glance.
ExpectedBehavior: SVG circle (customizable size, default 20px) with stroke showing health 0-100 as arc. Color coded: red (health 0-33), amber (34-66), green (67-100). At 0 health, ring is hidden but SVG box still occupies space (no layout shift). Transitions smoothly when health changes (0.5s ease). Optional center content (icon) rendered absolutely centered.
Notes: Reusable component. Used in StatusBar, ProjectCard, ProjectAssignedToMe, MultimodalWorkspace. Health to color mapping: health <= 33 → red (#ef4444), 34-66 → amber (#f59e0b), ≥ 67 → green (#22c55e). Animates: stroke-dashoffset and stroke color.
Permissions: Platform-admin only (isPlatformAdminUsername allowlist); debug shells are dev-gated

UserStory: As a translator, I want to understand which cells are dragging down project health, so that I can prioritize fixes.
ExpectedBehavior: Popover triggered by hover on health ring (delay 300ms, close delay 120ms) or on-click. Shows: (1) 'PROJECT HEALTH' label + percentage; (2) 'X% of cells need attention' summary (cells with decay above warn threshold, default 0.3); (3) Optional 'N cell(s) with stale source' row if staleSourceCount > 0; (4) 'Biggest drags' section listing top 8 cells sorted by descending decay (ascending health), each clickable to jump to cell if callback provided, each showing cell label and health %. If no cells need attention, shows 'No cells need attention.' message.
Notes: Receive healthByCell array (cellId, label, health) and calculate via useMemo: cells needing attention (health < attentionHealthCutoff), top 8 drags. warnThreshold defaults to 0.3. Popover content styled with 'neu-raised' design, rounded-2xl. Opens on hover with 300ms delay.
Permissions: Platform-admin only (isPlatformAdminUsername allowlist); debug shells are dev-gated

UserStory: As a user, I want a flexible status bar component that can display custom left and right content, so that different workspace views can show relevant info.
ExpectedBehavior: Minimal wrapper component rendering horizontal flex layout with three sections: left content (min-width flex-shrink-0), spacer (flex-1), right content (shrink-0). Passed as ReactNode props. Used for workspace-specific status displays.
Notes: Generic container; no inherent styling beyond layout. Text size: text-xs. Padding: px-4 py-1.5. Used to hold left/right slot content in workspace shell.
Permissions: Platform-admin only (isPlatformAdminUsername allowlist); debug shells are dev-gated

UserStory: As a platform operator, I want admin features to be restricted to allowlisted users, so that only authorized personnel can access sensitive endpoints.
ExpectedBehavior: usePlatformAdmin() hook checks current JWT via getAdminMe(jwt) API call at mount. Sets isAdmin state to true/false and loading state. AdminConsole route mounts with platform admin gate: if !loading && !isAdmin, redirects to /. Non-admin access to /admin navigates to / via Navigate component. Server enforces PLATFORM_ADMINS allowlist on every /api/v2/admin/* call (403 if not listed).
Notes: UX gate only; server is the real enforcer. Hook follows useOrg pattern with aliveRef guard for React StrictMode. Session loading state handled: if session still hydrating, stays loading=true until jwt resolves. Non-admin users don't see admin nav entries because isAdmin stays false.
Permissions: Platform-admin only (isPlatformAdminUsername allowlist)

UserStory: As a user, I want browser history (back/forward popover) to show descriptive page titles, so that I can navigate to specific pages by name.
ExpectedBehavior: deriveNavTitle(pathname) maps routes to human-readable labels: '/' → 'Home', '/projects' → 'Projects', '/admin' → 'Admin console', '/project/:id' → 'Editor', '/project/:id/settings' → 'Project settings', '/project/:id/rules' → 'Checks & rules', etc. Unknown routes title-case the last path segment. Used by NavHistoryControls popover to label history entries.
Notes: Provisional label from URL alone (no data lookups). Pages upgrade their title via useNavHistoryTitle() hook once rich data (project name, file name) loads. Covers admin + debug routes explicitly (/admin, /debug implied by fallback).
Permissions: Platform-admin only (isPlatformAdminUsername allowlist); debug shells are dev-gated
